item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox have been shopping Jarren Duran at the GM Meetings, according to the Boston Globe’s Peter Abraham.

The Red Sox were open to moving Duran last winter, but they never received the right offer. They’ll find the offers even more underwhelming this time around, but it seems likely that he’ll be traded anyway. The Red Sox could then pursue Randy Arozarena or Seiya Suzuki as an upgrade as a left fielder/designated hitter. Duran has two seasons left before free agency. He was a big disappointment in hitting .207/.266/.361 in 2026, but he has accrued 14.3 bWAR while posting a 110 OPS+ over the last three seasons combined.

item.title: [CBS Sports] MLB rumors: Yankees eye Alec Bohm, Tarik Skubal books more meetings, plus Nationals, Orioles, Mariners, more
item.dc:creator: Dayn Perry

item.content:encoded:
The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 1 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22. As for the present moment, the General Manager Meetings in Las Vegas are underway, and since there may not be any Winter Meetings this offseason (thanks to the lockout), the GMs' pow-wow could instead be a locus of activity.
Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace and the ongoing GM Meetings, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Wednesday's supply just below.
Yankees interested in Bohm
The New York Yankees are eyeing an upgrade at third base given the prolonged struggles of Ryan McMahon, and free agent Alec Bohm may be a potential target for GM Brian Cashman, according to the New York Post. Bohm, 30, is coming off a subpar walk year for the Philadelphia Phillies, but he has a career OPS+ of 101 overall. He also fared much better in the second half, and his season-long numbers were dragged down by a terrible April. Bohm is not much of a fielder these days, but the Yankees may be willing to live with that if they determine he can provide an offensive upgrade.
As for McMahon, Cashman already conceded to looking for a replacement.
"He's signed through next year for us, but I definitely know we need to improve production in a lot of different spots on the club if we can," he told reporters on Tuesday. "So we'll be open-minded to finding what we can run into if it's there."
Skubal market continues to take shape
The market for ace Tarik Skubal, far and away the top free agent available this offseason, continues to pick up steam, and it may be that he signs his next contract before the owners lock out the players on Dec. 1. The Los Angeles Dodgers, who traded for Skubal leading up to the deadline, the New York Mets, the Chicago Cubs, and the San Diego Padres are known to have varying levels of interest in Skubal. Now, the New York Post reports, the Toronto Blue Jays have entered the fray and emerged as Skubal suitors.
As for the Dodgers, they indeed plan to meet with Skubal, GM Brandon Gomes said. Mets top executive David Stearns, also speaking to reporters, emphasized that he and the club are willing to offer lengthy contracts to pitchers but that circumstances matter. That, in theory, should allay fears that he's not prepared to make a significant offer.
Padres hoping for Pivetta reunion
The San Diego Padres not long ago declined their club option on right-handed starter Nick Pivetta. However, they may not mean a parting of ways for club and player. Padres lead decision-maker AJ Preller on Tuesday told reporters, including Marty Caswell, that the team hopes to work out a new agreement with Pivetta so that he can return to San Diego for the 2027 season and perhaps beyond. Pivetta enjoyed a standout season in 2025, but his 2026, while excellent while on the mound, consisted of just eight regular-season starts because of elbow problems.
Nationals getting trade interest in Dylan Crews
Dylan Crews, the 24-year-old outfielder for the Washington Nationals, has yet to reach the potential that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick in 2023. However, that ceiling is still there, and Crews is obviously young enough to realize his promise. Speaking of Crews, the Athletic reports that multiple teams have approached the Nats about Crews' availability in trade and that the Nats have not declared him off-limits. That of course doesn't mean a trade will happen, but a change of scenery for Crews may indeed be a winter possibility.
Mariners favoring Suzuki over Arozarena reunion
Outfielder Randy Arozarena was the Seattle Mariners' top player last season, and now he's a free agent. The M's, though, may not be interested in bringing back Arozarena and instead may be targeting fellow free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki, the Seattle Times reports. Each veteran outfielder will be going into his age-32 season in 2027, and each produced at a high level in 2026.
Orioles not inclined to tear it down
After missing the playoffs in back-to-back seasons and trading away catcher Adley Rutschman leading up to the 2026 deadline, the Baltimore Orioles seem like a teardown candidate on paper. However, president of baseball operations Mike Elias batted down talk of a major roster makeover. "A lot of our key, core players are very unlikely to go anywhere," Elias told the media, including the Baltimore Banner, at the GM Meetings.
That presumably means that coveted shortstop Gunnar Henderson, among other notable names, won't be going anywhere this winter.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Seiya Suzuki Pens Emotional Message to Cubs Fans
item.dc:creator: Adam Martin
item.description: Free-agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki has penned an emotional message to Chicago Cubs fans as he prepares to depart the organization. After spending his first five MLB seasons with the Cubs, Suzuki is now a free agent, and he is expected to command a huge contract on the open market, which could potentially spell an end to his time with the Cubs. With Suzuki likely on the move, he has now taken to his social media to thank the Cubs fans for everything they did for him the last five years in Chicago
item.content:encoded:
Free-agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki has penned an emotional message to Chicago Cubs fans as he prepares to depart the organization.
After spending his first five MLB seasons with the Cubs, Suzuki is now a free agent, and he is expected to command a huge contract on the open market, which could potentially spell an end to his time with the Cubs.
With Suzuki likely on the move, he has now taken to his social media to thank the Cubs fans for everything they did for him the last five years in Chicago.
Seiya Suzuki Issues Statement to Cubs Fans
Taking to his social media, Suzuki shared a message with the Cubs fans on his Instagram.
“To all the Cubs fans, Thank you for another incredible season, and thank you so much for all the support and love you’ve shown me throughout this year. I truly appreciate it. First and foremost, thank you for five amazing years. I’m grateful for everything — the beautiful ballpark, the best fans in baseball, the incredible teammates I’ve had the privilege of playing alongside, and the opportunity to wear a Cubs uniform. These are memories I will always cherish. Thank you also for welcoming my family with so much kindness. My family has come to love Chicago just as much as I do. We are truly grateful for all the love and support you’ve shown us. I know there are still many things ahead, and I look forward to sharing more with you all when the time comes. Once again, thank you for all the support this season. It means more to me than words can express. Thank you, Cubs fans!”
Where Will Seiya Suzuki Go?
While it’s still possible that the Cubs could re-sign Suzuki, at this point, it seems more likely that he will be moving on.
Suzuki is expected to command a free-agent deal worth more than $100 million, with teams such as the Toronto Blue Jays, Seattle Mariners, Baltimore Orioles, and Philadelphia Phillies among the potential fits to add the slugger in free agency this winter once he turns down his Qualifying Offer.

item.content:encoded:
カブスからＦＡとなった鈴木誠也外野手（３２）とホワイトソックス・村上宗隆内野手（２６）の共闘は実現するのか。米老舗誌「スポーツ・イラストレーテッド」の電子版「ＯＮ ＳＩ」は現地時間の１０日、「ホワイトソックスは鈴木誠也獲得で大型補強を試みるべき」との記事を掲載した。
同記事は「ホワイトソックスは２０２６年の快進撃のシーズン中、レギュラーの外野手陣をルーキーで固め、そのうち２人がア・リーグ新人王の投票で票を獲得した。球宴に選出されたトリスタン・ピーターズにとっては、それほど驚くべきことではなかった。一方、サム・アントナッチは、内野手出身にもかかわらず、あらゆる面で完璧なプレーを見せ、ファンのお気に入りとなった」と今季を振り返った。
その上で「ホワイトソックスが次のレベルを目指すなら右翼の守備を強化する必要があるだろう。資金に余裕がある彼らは、解決策を北へわずか８マイル（約１３キロ）の場所に求めるだけで済むかもしれない」と同じシカゴのチームに目を向けた。そしてＦＡとなった鈴木に対し「カブスは彼にクオリファイング・オファーを提示したが、応じる可能性は低い。何しろ、そのポジションのＦＡの中で最高のＷＡＲを記録した選手が、応じるはずがないからだ」と指摘。
今季の鈴木は打率２割７分、出塁率３割６分８厘、長打率４割７分３厘、２６本塁打、８６打点を記録。その観点から同誌は「ホワイトソックスの中軸打者として理想的な選手」とし「多くの強打者と同様に三振が多い傾向はあるものの出塁率が高く、得点を稼げるのであれば、それは許容範囲内だ」とも補足した。
そうなれば、最大の焦点はホワイトソックスが鈴木を球団史上初の１億ドル（約１５８億円）契約の選手にしたいと考えているかどうかだ。記事では「彼は３２歳だが、少なくともそれだけの金額を要求するだろう。ほとんどのファンは、その契約はもっと若くて将来性のある選手に与えられることを望んでいるはずだ」と解説している。
とはいえ「ホワイトソックスが鈴木の獲得について少なくとも問い合わせをしないのは、怠慢と言えるだろう」とも言い切る。最後に「今季右翼を守ったモンゴメリーの活躍は素晴らしい話だが、球団はそろそろこの若手中心のチームでどこまで行けるか真剣に考えるべき時だ」と訴え、ホワイトソックス・鈴木誕生の必要性を強調した。

item.title: [CBS Sports] MLB rumors: Mets to meet with Tarik Skubal, Braves' Ronald Acuña Jr. plan, plus Blue Jays, Cubs, Red Sox, more
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa

item.content:encoded:
This is an important week on the . First and foremost, it is awards week. Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart were . The Managers of the Year will be announced Tuesday, Cy Youngs and Relievers of the Year will be announced Wednesday, and finally the MVPs will be announced Thursday.
Also, the GM Meetings are this week in Las Vegas. The GM Meetings are not the Winter Meetings in terms of the sheer volume of rumors and transactions, but they do usually provide some news. There could be more than usual this year given the near certainty of a lockout on Dec. 1, which would also mean there are no Winter Meetings. This may be the only time everyone is in the same room this winter. .
We've already ranked the top 50 free agents and the top 25 trade candidates.
With that in mind, here are Tuesday's hot stove rumors.
Mets will meet with Skubal
The Mets have a meeting scheduled with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the clear top free agent avaiable this offseason, later this week, reports the New York Post. Skubal will meet with teams in California, presumably at the offices of agent Scott Boras. Owner Steve Cohen is expected to push for Skubal, according to SNY; president of baseball operations David Stearns has long been reluctant to sign big-money, long-term deals for pitchers, though pitchers of Skubal's caliber are rarely available. The Mets are also seeking first base help and bullpen reinforcements.
Nolan McLean and Christian Scott are the only locks for New York's 2027 rotation at the moment. Justin Hagenman, Sean Manaea, Kodai Senga, Zac Thornton, and Jonah Tong are next in line to make starts. Tylor Megill is expected back from Tommy John surgery early next year as well. The Mets have some depth but clearly need more impact.
Blue Jays interested in Lowe
The Blue Jays are among the teams with interest in free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Sportsnet. Ernie Clement, Toronto's primary second baseman in 2026, crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility man who plays regularly at different positions. Josh Smith is the team's other second base option.
Lowe would bring needed power to a team that finished dead last in home runs this past season and had just one player, Kazuma Okamoto (33), clear 15 home runs. Only four Blue Jays hit even 10 homers. Also, Toronto's lineup is mostly right-handed. Lowe would add power and also a lefty bat to provide balance. .
Rotation help a 'top priority' for White Sox
Adding rotation help is a "top priority," White Sox GM Chris Getz said during an MLB Network Radio interview on Tuesday. "We're going to exhaust the starter market, both free agency -- we'll take a look -- along with trades. That is our top priority," Getz said. He also confirmed that Grant Taylor, the team's postseason closer, will move into the rotation. Hagen Smith will remain in the bullpen.
The White Sox have solid enough rotation depth with Taylor joining Sean Burke, Luis Castillo, Anthony Kay, Davis Martin, David Sandlin, Noah Schultz, and perhaps Shane Smith and Drew Thorpe. There is room for improvement, though, particularly at the top. Chicago could use a bona fide ace, not that one is easy to acquire or abundantly available.
Padres have expressed interest in Skubal
Add the Padres to the list of teams that have shown interest in Skubal, reports MLB Network. San Diego has a major need in the rotation -- Joe Musgrove, who hasn't made a start since the 2024 postseason, and Randy Vásquez are their only rotation locks -- and a new ownership group that seems willing to spend in its first offseason.
. He is also a Scott Boras client, and, historically, top Boras clients take the largest contract offer regardless of team situation. That isn't to say the Padres are a bad situation. Not at all. They're a very good team that is in the postseason most years, plus they play in San Diego. Who doesn't love San Diego?
The Padres are also connected to several Japanese players, according to The Athletic. That includes MLB free agents Seiya Suzuki and Shota Imanaga, as well as players coming over from Nippon Professional Baseball, like third baseman Teruaki Sato.
Morejon prefers to stay in the bullpen
Free agent lefty Adrian Morejon is drawing interest as a starting pitcher, but he prefers to remain in the bullpen, according to The Athletic. Even during the season, there were rumblings that Morejon would like to be given a chance to start in 2027. He came up through the minors as a starter and only remained in the bullpen because he was so dominant in a late-inning role.
on the idea that he would move into the rotation. The belief within the game is that he has a chance to be an excellent starter, not just a back-end piece. Either way, Morejon is a very good pitcher, and at 28, he's also one of the youngest free agents available. He should have several peak years remaining.
Cubs hope to add three starters
, the Cubs hope to add three established starting pitchers this offseason, reports The Athletic. Of the nine pitchers to make at least nine starts for Chicago in 2027, seven are free agents. Only Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery (per ESPN), and Edward Cabrera, who had a 5.96 ERA and was demoted to the bullpen, remain.
Left-hander Justin Steele is expected back from UCL surgery next year, though he suffered a setback this summer and wasn't able to return as hoped in September. Others like Javier Assad and Jordan Wicks are depth options more than full-time rotation pieces. This free agent class offers plenty of second- and third-tier starters. That's where the Cubs are expected to shop.
Mets not interested in major overhaul
Unlike last offseason, the Mets are not interested in a major overhaul despite their disappointing year, reports MLB.com. The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. The only silver lining to the disappointing season was the ability to give a long runway to rookies like Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, both of whom finished in the top four of the Rookie of the Year voting.
The Mets went 83-79 in 2025 and missed the postseason on the final day of the season. They made significant changes last winter, most notably jettisoning stalwarts Pete Alonso and Brandon Nimmo, then had a worse season in 2026. In September, president of baseball operations David Stearns admitted that much turnover created an "uncapped downside scenario," which is executive-speak for "there was too much risk."
Braves will not move Acuña
Not surprisingly, the Braves are uninterested in moving former National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr., according to MLB Network. It does feel like Atlanta's offense has gone stale and that they could move a core piece, but it won't be Acuña, nor is it likely to be Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, or Matt Olson. Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are the more obvious players to move. Albies is entering the final season of his wildly team-friendly contract. Riley has six years remaining on his deal, which figures to make a move difficult.
Red Sox won't commit to Story at short
On Monday, Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow declined to commit to Trevor Story as his starting shortstop next season. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor, but any decisions like that are going to take place between Trevor and me far before I speak to anything publicly," Breslow told reporters, including the Boston Globe. Boston has in shortstop Franklin Arias, who is very likely to make his debut early next year. Arias could push Story into a utility role or off the team entirely.

item.content:encoded:
Let's switch gears for a moment from the pitchers I've been looking at and instead check out one of the top outfield free agents, former Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena.
No question, Arozarena has talent. He's a solid 3 or 4 WAR outfielder, generally good for 20+ home runs and 20+ stolen bases every year.
The red flag here is that 2026 was his best season. He batted .281/.381/.484 and led the American League in runs scored with 113, which was by far a career best (95 was his previous best). The .381 OBP was also a career high (except for .382 in only 76 PA in 2020).
Why a red flag? Because Arozarena's going to turn 32 in February. Would you give a guy like this a four-year deal coming off his best overall season? MLB Trade Rumors has him projected for four years and $100 million and The Athletic has Arozarena at essentially the same, four years and $108 million. Interestingly, the article in The Athletic has Seiya Suzuki projected at the same figures. Suzuki is a few months older than Arozarena, as is Ian Happ.
Both Happ and Suzuki are better defenders than Arozarena, and at those figures I'd certainly rather have either of the two departing Cubs back than Arozarena, despite Arozarena's base-stealing ability. Regarding that, here's an interesting note from the MLBTR article:
Arozarena runs quite a bit more than Suzuki but is actually a good bit slower in terms of average sprint speed; Statcast measures Suzuki with a sprint speed of 28 feet per second, in the 63rd percentile of big leaguers. Arozarena is at 27.1 ft/sec, down in the 40th percentile. He's an aggressive baserunner, however, and that's manifested in the form of six consecutive 20-steal seasons.
I imagine Jed Hoyer and his baseball ops staff will have a look at Arozarena, who's been a fan favorite everywhere he's been. Ultimately I think they'll probably pass on him, and that's what I would do as well.

item.content:encoded:
Left-hander Tarik Skubal is widely considered the top target for any team looking to add an ace this offseason. But one franchise that should be heavily involved in the starting pitching market this winter reportedly isn't expected to pursue the two-time Cy Young Award winner.
The Chicago Cubs "appear unlikely to enter the bidding war" for Skubal, according to The Athletic's Sahadev Sharma. However, Sharma also reported that Chicago "will at least check in on every other free-agent pitcher" this offseason.
Six pitchers who started at least nine games for the Cubs in 2026 are now free agents: Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, Colin Rea, David Peterson, Kevin Gausman, and Clay Holmes. Outfielders Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ are also expected to enter free agency. So, even if Skubal isn't in Chicago's offseason plans, the franchise will likely still be busy making moves this winter.
Which starting pitchers are more likely targets for the Cubs this offseason?
If the Cubs truly are willing to explore all free-agent pitching options besides Skubal this winter, there are still several impact arms available. One of Chicago's top targets could be San Diego Padres right-hander Michael King. The 31-year-old is expected to be one of the most coveted hurlers this offseason. And after the former Padre tossed seven shutout innings against Chicago in the playoffs, the Cubs may want to be on the other side of performances like that moving forward.
Right-hander Freddy Peralta is another big-name starter the Cubs could target. The 30-year-old pitched well for the Tampa Bay Rays down the stretch, and he previously played for Chicago manager Craig Counsell when they were both in Milwaukee. A reunion would give the Cubs a new ace for at least the next few years.
The Cubs could also look to re-sign one of their starters from this past season. Holmes, for example, is widely known as an effective ground-ball pitcher. With Chicago's superb infield defense, bringing the right-hander back could make a lot of sense. Regardless of who the Cubs end up signing, though, the team's 2027 rotation will likely look drastically different.
Justin Binkowski is a lifelong baseball fan returning to cover the sport he loves after spending nearly a decade writing about video games. Before his time as managing editor at Dot Esports, Binkowski attended King's College in Wilkes-Barre, PA, where he was also a relief pitcher on the school's baseball team. While in college, Binkowski was a media relations intern for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders during the 2014 season.

item.content:encoded:
Nov 9, 2026, 11:29 AM ET
The Atlanta Braves are "highly unlikely" to trade star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. this offseason, per Jon Morosi of MLB Network. Acuna is likely to hit free agency following the 2028 season, as Atlanta holds a club option for 2028 that they will almost certainly pick up. While the Braves may not be interested in paying Acuna what it would require to keep him past 2028, it appears that Atlanta is not entertaining moving him now ahead of 2027. Across 469 plate appearances in 2026, the 28-year-old hit .255/.345/.451 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 61 runs scored, and 21 stolen bases. While Acuna remains a productive player, he hasn't quite recaptured the magic of his 2023 season, when he hit 41 home runs and stole 73 bases. Injuries have been a huge part of the story, as Acuna Jr. missed significant time due to hamstring issues in 2026. If he can get back to full health, Acuna has as high a production upside as any player in baseball.--Will Brady
Source: MLB Network - Jon MorosiComments · Join ChatOpen App
More Recent News
Nov 9, 2026, 11:59 AM ET
Across 615 plate appearances in 2026, Atlanta Braves catcher Drake Baldwin hit .284/.358/.459 with 25 home runs, 79 RBI, 85 runs scored, and three stolen bases. The 25-year-old got off to a scorching-hot start to the season before suffering an oblique strain in mid-May that sidelined him for about a month. Baldwin struggled upon his return, hitting just .063 across 50 plate appearances in June after being reinserted into the Braves lineup. However, the young backstop bounced back and closed the season strong, hitting .315 with 10 home runs across 296 plate appearances after the All-Star break. Baldwin's underlying metrics supported his production at the plate, as he posted an excellent 50.9% hard-hit rate and kept his strikeout rate to a manageable 21.5%. Atlanta also frequently used him at designated hitter, both keeping his legs fresh and keeping him in the lineup on an everyday basis. Heading into 2027, Baldwin is in the conversation as the top catcher in fantasy baseball.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Nov 9, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Since his breakout season in 2024, Kansas City Royals left-hander Cole Ragans (elbow) has basically been a non-factor for fantasy managers. The 28-year-old pitched just 35 1/3 innings (eight starts) in 2026 before hitting the injured list with triceps and elbow soreness. Ragans initially attempted to rehab his arm, but he suffered a setback in June and ultimately underwent an internal brace procedure in July. As a result, Ragans missed the remainder of the 2026 season and will likely miss a significant chunk of 2027 as well. On the bright side, Ragans may finally be able to work his way back to full health and regain his peak form while he rehabs from the surgery. However, the talented southpaw is tough for fantasy managers to trust until he gets back on the mound and proves he can stay healthy for an extended stretch of time.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Nov 9, 2026, 11:39 AM ET
Pittsburgh Pirates shortstop Konnor Griffin had an up-and-down season as a rookie in 2026. The 20-year-old was productive for a very young player when healthy, hitting .272/.324/.404 with six home runs, 33 RBI, 43 runs scored, and 23 stolen bases. However, he spent a significant chunk of the season sidelined by two different injuries, first a flexor strain and then a finger injury. Griffin also struggled to hit for power even when he was on the field, posting just a 6.9% barrel rate and a 37.5% hard-hit rate. Still, Griffin managed to put together a respectable season as a rookie while battling injury issues. If he can get and stay fully healthy in 2027, Griffin could emerge as a true five-category difference-maker for fantasy managers. His profile carries some risk due to the unknown, but Griffin is an ultra-high-upside shortstop bet who could pay off for fantasy managers in a big way in 2027.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Nov 9, 2026, 11:22 AM ET
After initially opening the season in Triple-A, Boston Red Sox left-hander Payton Tolle emerged as arguably his team's best starting pitcher in 2026. Across 148 2/3 innings (26 starts) in the big leagues, Tolle recorded a 9-6 record with a 3.03 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 171 strikeouts. The 24-year-old averaged 96.2 miles per hour on his fastball and struck out 28.4% of the batters he faced while allowing just a 6.6% walk rate. Tolle also only allowed a .624 OPS against right-handed hitters, which will be key for him to continue as he makes his home starts in front of the Green Monster at Fenway Park. Heading into 2027, Tolle has all the makings of a fantasy ace, and he will likely come off the board very early in most drafts.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Bryan Woo a Bounce-Back Candidate in 2027


Will Brady




Nov 9, 2026, 11:14 AM ET
Seattle Mariners starting pitcher Bryan Woo had a disappointing year relative to expectations in 2026, recording a 12-10 record with a 4.01 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 175 strikeouts across 173 innings (30 starts). The 26-year-old's production dropped off across the board relative to his 2025 campaign, when he finished fifth in the American League Cy Young Award voting. However, there's plenty of reason for fantasy managers to believe in Woo's ability to bounce back in 2027. Much of Woo's ERA increase can be attributed to his 66.2% strand rate, which was significantly below his 73.4% career mark. Even in a down year, the young right-hander remained an excellent source of WHIP and a solid source of strikeouts, and he's also now logged back-to-back 30-start seasons. Heading into 2027, fantasy managers may want to look to buy low on Woo.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Catcher Testifies in Court Amid MLB Gambling Scandal


Keith Hernandez




Nov 9, 2026, 10:31 AM ET
Catcher Bo Naylor, a former teammate of Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, testified last Thursday at their sports-betting trial that he did not know gamblers could place bets on individual pitches until the criminal case arose, according to Larry Neumeister of The Associated Press. Clase and Ortiz pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges after they were filed a year ago. Prosecutors said the two pitchers accepted several thousand dollars in payments so sports gamblers could place bets on individual pitches, enabling the gamblers to pocket at least $460,000. Prosecutors say that Clase began giving information about his pitches to bettors in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Clase and Ortiz are both free on bail and are on non-disciplinary leave from the Guardians without pay while facing prosecution. Naylor testified that he was not close friends with either pitcher, and that he would frequently see Clase on his cellular phone in the locker room. Prosecutors have alleged that Clase sometimes broke MLB rules by communicating with gamblers during games.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Associated Press - Larry Neumeister
Cubs Unlikely to Enter Bidding War for Tarik Skubal


Keith Hernandez




Nov 9, 2026, 10:18 AM ET
The Chicago Cubs' priority this offseason is starting pitching, but The Athletic's Sahadev Sharma writes that it is unlikely that the Cubs will enter a bidding war for two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. The Cubs were aggressive in adding third baseman Alex Bregman to a five-year, $175 million deal last offseason, but they have shied away from the very top of the free-agent market in recent offseasons. Chicago has "shown no interest" in spending like the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets, and it will not be an exception this winter, when labor negotiations will muddy the waters for teams and their finances. The Cubs will, however, check in on other pitches, as they have just one pitcher with legitimate starting experience on their roster who is set to enter 2027 healthy. The goal for the Cubs is likely to bring in three starting pitchers. After their starters allowed the third-most home runs (142) in 2026, the Cubs will target pitchers with high ground-ball rates and/or a high strikeout rate. This means they will most likely attempt to bring back right-hander Clay Holmes, who led baseball with a 60.7% ground-ball rate. Two other potential free-agent fits could be Freddy Peralta and Michael King. For Skubal, it is going to take a large sum of money to secure his services long-term, and the Dodgers and Mets will be the front-runners.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Sahadev Sharma
Corbin Carroll has Offseason Elbow Surgery


Keith Hernandez




Nov 9, 2026, 10:09 AM ET
Arizona Diamondbacks outfielder Corbin Carroll (elbow) had offseason elbow surgery last Thursday to remove loose bodies, according to Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic. Carroll is expected to maintain a normal offseason program and should be a full-go for spring training next year. The All-Star outfielder and former National League Rookie of the Year said he felt "a little bit" of discomfort in his elbow during the season, but it worsened last week. He said he has a minimally invasive NanoScope procedure, which is the same one that left-hander Tarik Skubal had when he was still with the Detroit Tigers last season that allowed him to return from the injured list in only six weeks. Carroll said he is hoping to start swinging a bat again at the start of December. Piecoro notes that the bigger issue for Carroll in 2026 was his back. He is trying to put himself in better positions in the weight room to avoid similar problems in the future. The 26-year-old also had a hamate procedure on his hand at the start of spring training, and he hit .239/.328/.467 with 22 homers, 33 doubles, and 17 triples while stealing 21 bases in 582 at-bats. It was definitely a drop after Carroll had 31 homers, 84 RBI, and 32 steals in 2025, but he has at least 22 homers and 21 stolen bases in each of the last four years.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Arizona Republic - Nick Piecoro
Seiya Suzuki Receives Qualifying Offer From Cubs


Keith Hernandez




Nov 6, 2026, 11:14 AM ET
As expected, outfielder Seiya Suzuki received a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Chicago Cubs, according to Joel Sherman of the New York Post. Suzuki will almost certainly decline the offer and enter the free-agent market this winter as one of the top free-agent outfield bats available. It remains to be seen if Chicago is serious about re-signing the 32-year-old, who had another strong season in 2026 in his fifth year in the majors, slashing .270/.368/.473 with an .841 OPS, 26 home runs, 86 RBI, 96 runs scored, and three stolen bases in 143 games across 634 plate appearances. Suzuki sold out for power in 2025 with a career-low .245 batting average (140-for-571), but he did produce career highs in home runs (32) and RBI (103) in 151 regular-season games played. In addition to being a consistent power bat in the outfield, Suzuki has graded out well defensively in right field, which will make him even more attractive on the open market this offseason. If he declines the Cubs' qualifying offer (he should), the Cubs will receive draft-pick compensation if he signs elsewhere.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Post - Joel Sherman
Jacob Young, Nationals Agree to Four-Year Extension


Keith Hernandez




Nov 6, 2026, 11:06 AM ET
Outfielder Jacob Young and the Washington Nationals agreed to a four-year, $23 million contract extension on Friday that includes an $8 million option for a fifth season, a source familiar with the deal told Robert Murray of FanSided. The deal helps the Nats avoid salary arbitration for the first time with Young. The 27-year-old is more glove and speed than bat, as he is considered one of the better defensive center fielders in the game. Although the former seventh-rounder in 2021 from the University of Florida does not have much power at the plate, he does have enough speed to make him fantasy-relevant in deeper leagues. Young stole a career-high 33 bases for the Nats in his first full season in 2024 and has at least 15 steals in the last two seasons. The 2026 campaign was one of his better showings at the plate, hitting .252/.318/.390 with a career-high .707 OPS, a career-high 10 home runs, 50 RBI, 57 runs scored, and 18 stolen bases in 140 games across 471 plate appearances. Fantasy managers seeking power from an outfielder will want to avoid Young, as he has hit just 15 home runs in his four big-league seasons since debuting with Washington in 2023.--Keith Hernandez
Source: FanSided - Robert Murray
Albert Pujols to Interview for Astros' Managerial Job


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 10:30 PM ET
Future Hall of Fame first baseman Albert Pujols will interview for the Houston Astros' managerial vacancy on Thursday, sources told Alden Gonzalez of ESPN. The Astros named former St. Louis Cardinals executive Randy Flores as their new general manager five days ago. Flores spent eight years in the big leagues before joining St. Louis' front office, with five of those years spent as Pujols' teammate in St. Louis, including a World Series championship in 2006. Pujols has made it clear that he has a desire to manage in the big leagues, and he won a championship in the Dominican winter league in his first season leading the Leones del Escogido in January of 2025 while also serving as the skipper for the Dominican Republic in this year's World Baseball Classic, where his squad lost to the United States in the semifinals. Pujols was a finalist for the managerial openings in the last hiring cycle with the Los Angeles Angels and San Diego Padres. New York Yankees bench coach Brad Ausmus is also among those being considered by the Astros for their managerial position.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN.com - Alden Gonzalez
Padres Extend Qualifying Offer to Adrian Morejon


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 10:10 PM ET
The San Diego Padres extended a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer to left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon, according to the New York Post's Joel Sherman. The 27-year-old hard-throwing southpaw is expected to decline the offer and become one of the top relievers available in his prime. Morejon has until Nov. 17 to accept or decline the offer. The Padres chose not to extend a qualifying offer to first baseman Ty France. Morejon, who hits triple digits on the radar gun regularly with his fastball and has pinpoint control, had a strong 2.83 ERA over 76 relief outings this year after posting a 2.08 ERA in 2025. If Morejon declines the offer, as expected, and signs elsewhere, the Padres would receive a compensatory draft pick. The Padres will have one of the better bullpens in baseball again in 2027, even if Morejon does not return, but they are definitely interested in a reunion. Morejon also expressed a desire to return at the end of the season. "Everybody knows that," Morejon said of his desire to return. "My agent knows that. It's not really in my hands right now." Morejon could have a chance to be a full-time closer if he tests the market, though, but in San Diego, he would remain a late-inning setup man in front of Mason Miller.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Post - Joel Sherman
Jake Bauers Receives Qualifying Offer From Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 10:02 PM ET
First baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers received a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer from the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, according to Joel Sherman of the New York Post. Of the eight players who were extended qualifying offers by their respective teams, Bauers is the most surprising. The 31-year-old left-handed slugger had a strong year in 2026 and definitely played a key role in helping the Brewers capture their first-ever World Series title, but coming into this season, he had never produced more than 12 home runs in a single season in six years in the big leagues. In 144 games and 578 plate appearances with the Brew Crew during the regular season, Bauers hit .266/.389/.484 with a career-best .874 OPS, 26 home runs, 86 RBI, 93 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases. He had a career slash line of .208/.302/.361 at the end of the 2024 season and came close to hanging up his cleats. Bauers tapped into a side we had never seen before this year, walking at a 16.3% clip, with only six qualified hitters having a higher wRC+ than Bauers. He was named the National League Championship Series MVP and could serve as the Brewers' primary first baseman in 2027 if he accepts the qualifying offer, which he is expected to do.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Post - Joel Sherman
Ryan Jeffers Receives Qualifying Offer From Twins


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 9:47 PM ET
Catcher Ryan Jeffers received a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Minnesota Twins, according to Dan Hayes of The Athletic. Jeffers has until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline it. Jeffers, who is about to enter his age-30 campaign, has been one of the more productive catchers in baseball in the last few seasons. The former second-rounder in 2018 from the University of North Carolina at Wilmington played in only 92 games due to injuries in the first half of the year in his seventh season with the Twins in 2026, but he was still very productive, slashing .256/.353/.461 with an .814 OPS, 14 home runs, 56 RBI, 49 runs scored, and a stolen base in 369 plate appearances. Most players who are extended a qualifying offer end up rejecting it to seek more riches on the open market, but it could be hard for Jeffers to turn this one-year deal down. If Jeffers turns the offer down and goes to the open market, he will be one of the most sought-after offensive-minded catchers of the offseason. Jeffers had a career-high 21 home runs and 64 RBI a couple of seasons ago in 2024, but he also hit just .226 that year with a .300 on-base percentage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Dan Hayes
Pirates Extend Qualifying Offer to Brandon Lowe


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 9:28 PM ET
The Pittsburgh Pirates extended a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer to second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Alex Stumpf. Lowe has until Nov. 17 to accept or deny it. If he denies and signs elsewhere, the Pirates will get a draft pick. The Pirates and Lowe can still negotiate other contracts. It is only the third time since the inception of the qualifying offer in 2012 that the Pirates have chosen to offer it to a player. Pittsburgh acquired the power-hitting second baseman last offseason in a three-team deal that involved the Tampa Bay Rays and Houston Astros. Not only did Lowe fortify his defense at second base in 2026 to become a Gold Glove finalist for the first time in his career, but he also played in a career-high 150 games while recording a career-best 5.4 wins above replacement. Offensively, he flourished in the Steel City, picking up 96 RBI and an .824 OPS while leading all second basemen with 35 home runs. Lowe is expected to decline the one-year qualifying offer for a more lucrative multi-year deal on the open market. The two-time All-Star now has two straight 30-homer seasons (three in his career) and has some of the best pop among second basemen, but it remains to be seen if he will be able to stay healthy in his 10th year in the big leagues in 2027.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Alex Stumpf
Nov 3, 2026, 9:14 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays right-handed reliever Edwin Uceta (shoulder) underwent an arthroscopic procedure on his right shoulder in October and will miss at least the first couple of months of the 2027 season, president of baseball operations Erik Neander told Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times. Uceta was set to enter the 2026 campaign as Tampa's primary ninth-inning option, but that all changed when he dealt with a right-shoulder impingement and never pitched for the Rays at all last season. Bryan Baker ended up taking over closing duties for Tampa and led all of baseball with 41 saves and a 1.44 ERA to help the team get back to the World Series, where they lost in five games to the Milwaukee Brewers. Uceta will now miss the start of next season as well, and when he returns, he will most likely be relegated to a high-leverage setup role in front of Baker. The 28-year-old Dominican hurler combined to go 12-3 with a 2.98 ERA (2.98 FIP), 1.04 WHIP, six saves, 160 strikeouts, and 35 walks in 117 2/3 relief innings over 100 appearances out of the bullpen in his first two seasons for the Rays in 2024 and 2025. There is no guarantee that Uceta will be as dominant a high-leverage bullpen arm when he returns from his shoulder issues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tampa Bay Times - Marc Topkin
Jazz Chisholm Jr. Not Expected Back in the Bronx


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:58 PM ET
ESPN's Jorge Castillo writes that both New York Yankees infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. and outfielder Trent Grisham "are as good as gone" for next season, so the Yankees will need to figure out second base and center field. Chisholm was one of the notable names this year not to be given a $23.15 million qualifying offer, so the Yankees will not receive draft-pick compensation when he leaves in free agency. Chisholm was an All-Star for the second time in his career in 2025 in his first full season with the Bombers, clubbing 31 home runs, driving in 80 runs, and stealing 31 bases in only 130 regular-season games, but he could not match that production in his seventh year in the big leagues. The 28-year-old left-handed slugger struggled to a .231 batting average (109-for-471) with 19 home runs, 55 RBI, and a 29.5% strikeout rate in 532 regular-season plate appearances, but he did manage to steal a career-high 41 bases. On the open market this offseason, Chisholm will be one of the most coveted power/speed threats among position players, but a move away from New York's short porch in right field could hurt his overall power ceiling in fantasy baseball.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN.com - Jorge Castillo
Teoscar Hernandez an Obvious Trade Candidate for Dodgers


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:45 PM ET
ESPN's Buster Olney writes that veteran outfielder Teoscar Hernandez is the Los Angeles Dodgers' most obvious trade candidate this offseason as they look to reshape their position-player group to get younger and more athletic. As Hernandez gets older and his defensive skills decline, there is no place for him at designated hitter in L.A., with the presence of Shohei Ohtani. Not only does Hernandez's defense in left field continue to decline, but he was also a disappointment at the plate in 2026 after signing a three-year, $66 million contract with the Blue last offseason. The 34-year-old Dominican native saw a sharp drop in power and hit .267/.334/.425 with a .759 OPS, 16 home runs, 64 RBI, 66 runs scored, five stolen bases, 135 strikeouts, and 42 walks in 125 games played and 491 plate appearances during the regular season. The two-time All-Star hit a combined 58 home runs and drove in 188 runs during the regular season in his first two years with the Dodgers while helping them win back-to-back championships. The writing is on the wall for Hernandez to be traded away, which would be a big hit to his fantasy value.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN - Buster Olney
Yankees Plan to Bring Giancarlo Stanton to Spring Training


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:36 PM ET
There has been speculation as to whether the New York Yankees would cut oft-injured outfielder/designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton this offseason, but YES Network's Jack Curry said that the Yankees will bring Stanton to spring training next year to see what he has left in the tank. If the 36-year-old five-time All-Star and former MVP struggles in spring training or is still injured, the Yankees could move on then. He is entering the final year of his 13-year, $325 million deal with the Yankees and is owed $15 million in 2027 ($10 million buyout), with a $15 million club option for the 2028 season, which is expected to be declined. General manager Brian Cashman said that Stanton finished the 2026 season healthy, but he managed to play in only 24 games in his 17th year in the league while slashing .256/.302/.422 with a .724 OPS, three home runs, 14 RBI, eight runs scored, and a 29:6 K:BB in 96 plate appearances. In 2025, Stanton played in only 77 games. Stanton has become a major injury liability and could find himself on the free-agent market early next year if he cannot get back on the field and stay there.--Keith Hernandez
Source: YES Network - Jack Curry
MLB Proposes Delaying Salary Cap Until 2028


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:26 PM ET
Major League Baseball proposed postponing the implementation of a salary cap until the 2028 season on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Jeff Passan, as the current collective bargaining agreement approaches its Dec. 1 expiration. The league has pressed forward with its pursuit of a cap and floor despite the Players Association voicing its objection to any cap. The $258.2 million cap and $180.2 million floor that MLB projected for 2028 were higher than the $245.3 million and $171.2 million numbers that the league proposed as its original cap-and-floor offer for 2027. MLB also proposed giving $282 million in competitive balance tax proceeds to players in cash payments, according to sources. Union officials have said that players would lose more than $1 billion over the life of the league's proposal if they agreed to a cap. The last time MLB formally proposed a cap-and-floor system in 1994, players went on strike for 232 days, and the World Series was canceled. Under the 2028 cap-and-floor projections, 12 teams, including the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, would need to increase their payrolls to reach the floor. Eight teams carried payrolls that would have been in excess of the ceiling. The MLBPA has proposed maintaining the current framework of the league's financial system while increasing spending, and the union has also asked for a surge in the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1.5 million and free agency for players 30 and older after five years of major-league service, not six.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN.com - Jeff Passan

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Looking For A Match In A Steven Kwan Trade
item.dc:creator: Mark Polishuk
item.description: “As we sit here today, we’re expecting Steven Kwan to be a big part of a contending team next year,” Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti told reporters during the team’s season wrap-up press conference after the ALCS. item.content:encoded:
“As we sit here today, we’re expecting Steven Kwan to be a big part of a contending team next year,” Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti told reporters during the team’s season wrap-up press conference after the ALCS. This was something less than a confirmation that Kwan will be back with the Guards in 2027, and it could indeed be that Kwan’s “contending team” plays somewhere other than Cleveland.
The Guardians have made a habit of winning without much offense in recent years, and the club’s collective 97 wRC+ (ranking 22nd in baseball) in 2026 was no exception. Trading one of their most dependable hitters therefore doesn’t make too much sense on paper for the Guardians, especially when the outfield in particular has been a weak link, and Kwan adds a ton of defensive value beyond his contributions at the plate.
That said, trading an increasingly expensive veteran a year or two prior to free agency has long been a favored tactic of the Guardians’ front office (not to mention other consistently small-market teams like the Brewers or Rays). Kwan is projected to earn $11.3MM in his final season of arbitration eligibility, before he is slated to hit the open market next winter. Unless Kwan is open to a very team-friendly extension a la Jose Ramirez, chances are Kwan will be playing for another team by 2028 anyway, so trading him now would allow Cleveland to again restock the roster for both 2027 and the future.
Even as the Guardians have been in playoff contention, there has already been a lot of trade buzz surrounding Kwan in the past couple of years. The Phillies, Padres, Dodgers, Blue Jays, and Reds were all reportedly interested in Kwan at the 2025 trade deadline, so Antonetti and company might already have an idea of what suitors are willing to offer for the two-time All-Star. MLB Trade Rumors ranked Kwan 11th on our list of the offseason’s top 40 candidates.
It is also worth noting that Kwan’s bat has been somewhat inconsistent. Kwan posted a 122 wRC+ in his 2022 rookie season, but subsequently delivered a 99 wRC+ in 2023, a 130 wRC+ in 2024, a 98 wRC+ in 2025, and then a 114 wRC+ this year. Even in 2026, Kwan had a Jekyll-and-Hyde season — he had an ugly .614 OPS over his first 354 plate appearances, but then rebounded for an .875 OPS in his 283 PA after the All-Star break.
This streaky hitting is perhaps par for the course for a player who makes very little hard contact and hits for very little power. Kwan’s game is built around taking walks (and his 13.3% walk rate in 2026 was a career high) and putting the ball in play almost as often as any player in baseball. Apart from the offensive skillset, Kwan won four Gold Gloves for his elite work in left field from 2022-25, and he delivered more strong glovework in both left and center field in 2026 when the Guards basically split Kwan’s time between the two positions.
The looming lockout adds another wrinkle to Cleveland’s plans, and perhaps adds to the possibility that Kwan might not be dealt at all. According to MLB Network’s Jon Morosi, rival teams could be “unlikely” to trade prospects prior to December 1 for players with only one year of team control, simply because a lengthy lockout could cut into the 2027 season itself.
One work-around for clubs like the Guardians would be to offer Kwan for another player with one year of control, in more of a classic need-for-need baseball trade than as a way of amassing younger talent. Since this doesn’t meet the Guardians’ preferred model of deals, the Guards could prefer to just keep Kwan at least through a lockout, and see how things stand once the offseason eventually gets back underway.
With all of this in mind, let’s break down the other 29 teams to see who lines up best as a possible Kwan suitor…
Not Likely
The Rockies and Angels are rebuilding. The Cardinals and Nationals performed better than expected in what was expected to be a rebuilding year in 2026, but acquiring Kwan doesn’t really fit what either team is planning for 2027. The Guardians probably wouldn’t automatically hang up the phone if the Royals, Twins, Tigers, or White Sox came calling on Kwan, but barring a real knockout offer, it’s hard to imagine Cleveland moving Kwan to a division rival.
The Brewers have Jackson Chourio and Garrett Mitchell in left and center, so the World Series champs have no real need for Kwan. The A’s have Tyler Soderstrom in left field and Henry Bolte and Denzel Clarke in center field, plus the Athletics have a much bigger need for pitching help. The Red Sox also have a loaded outfield in Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilyer Abreu, and if anything, will be looking to trade from their outfield mix by moving Jarren Duran. The Mets have Juan Soto, Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing as their starting outfield, and moving Soto into a full-time DH role to accommodate Kwan probably isn’t happening.
The Past Trade Suitors
Of the five teams previously linked to Kwan, two seem less likely to keep exploring a trade. Josue De Paula’s emergence is only further crowding the Dodgers’ outfield, to the point that Teoscar Hernandez is another plausible outfield trade chip as the team looks to create lineup space for De Paula. The Reds could badly use Kwan to help stabilize their shaky outfield, but giving up a significant trade package for a player with one year of control might not align with Cincinnati’s own approach as a lower-spending team.
The Blue Jays could use Kwan in either left or center field, if Anthony Santander is kept as a primary DH or Brett Bateman is used more in a part-time role than as an everyday outfielder. Toronto figures to be exploring the outfield market but might prefer a slugger, given how the Jays lacked in the power department last year. The Phillies have power but need more contact from their lineup, and Kwan is a big defensive upgrade to Philadelphia’s outfield, so Brandon Marsh or Justin Crawford could be moved over to right field to accommodate Kwan. The Padres have a big hole to fill in left field and Kwan would be an ideal fit.
Swinging a deal for Kwan is absolutely within the purview for any of these latter three teams, who are in clear win-now mode. For what it’s worth, Antonetti has completed multiple trades with both Padres president of baseball ops A.J. Preller and Blue Jays GM Ross Atkins over the years.
Other Candidates
Astros: The Astros are badly in need of both outfielders and left-handed hitters. Yordan Alvarez is provisionally projected for left field duty given Houston’s infield surplus, but it is way more likely that the slugger is more or less an everyday DH. Of the Astros’ infielders, Jeremy Pena is also a free agent after 2027 but the Astros have no obvious way of replacing Pena at shortstop unless Carlos Correa is moved back to the position. That means a fun Pena-for-Kwan deal probably isn’t realistic, but could a trade involving Kwan and Isaac Paredes be a possibility?
Braves: Mike Yastrzemski and Jurickson Profar are lined up for platoon duty in left field, except Yaz struggled in 2026 and Profar missed the entire season on a PED suspension. Since it’s possible Profar could be released entirely, acquiring Kwan makes sense for the Braves as a way to stabilize left field, as Yastrzemski could then be used in right field whenever Ronald Acuna Jr. needs a DH day.
Cubs: Pete Crow-Armstrong has center field locked up in Wrigleyville, but the left field spot is wide open since Ian Happ is a free agent. With Seiya Suzuki also hitting the open market, Chicago is expected to use Matt Shaw for one corner outfield vacancy, but if both Happ and Suzuki leave, bringing a veteran like Kwan on board is a logical move that will keep the Cubs’ elite defense in place.
Diamondbacks: Arizona has a stated need for left-handed hitting. Lars Nootbaar is lined up as the regular left fielder but could be moved to DH, or Kwan could play center field. The D’Backs want to find at-bats for Jordan Lawlar and Ryan Waldschmidt, but the open DH spot gives the team some flexibility in pursuing someone like Kwan, if a trade can be worked out with Cleveland.
Giants: Casey Schmitt and Drew Gilbert project as the regulars in left and center field, assuming Marcelo Mayer plays well enough at second base to keep Schmitt in a corner outfield role. It’s not the greatest of combinations and Kwan would certainly be a big upgrade, but the Giants may be more apt to spend their trade capital to address larger needs on the pitching staff. San Francisco has been unwilling to invest heavily in pitching, so if the team prefers to acquire arms via trade, the Giants could spend on a bigger free agent bat in the outfield.
Mariners: Returning to Morosi’s report, would something like a Kwan-for-Logan Gilbert deal make sense? Gilbert’s projected arb salary of $15.4MM is higher than Kwan’s, but he’d be a high-end way for the Guardians to bolster an already-strong rotation. Realistically, Gilbert is less of a fit for Cleveland than Kwan would be for Seattle, as left fielder Randy Arozarena is expected to leave in free agency.
Marlins: Kwan would be a nice add for a club looking for corner outfield options, plus Kwan can fill in as a center fielder since Jakob Marsee is expected to miss some time early in the season while he recovers from internal brace surgery. The Marlins have been a borderline contender in each of the last two seasons but making a trade for an All-Star player with one year of team control might not be something the club is ready or willing to do just yet.
Orioles: Baltimore is in the awkward position of being a little crowded in terms of position players, but with a lot of uncertainty about basically the entire group save for Pete Alonso. To this end, the O’s are reportedly open to at least discussing everyone but Alonso, which opens the door for the Guardians and other teams to explore all manner of interesting trade possibilities. Acquiring Kwan would make for a first-choice outfield entirely comprised of left-handed hitters (with Kwan joining Colton Cowser and Dylan Beavers), but that might be a secondary concern for the Orioles behind the bigger-picture desire to improve their average, defense, and contact hitting.
Pirates: Bryan Reynolds and Oneil Cruz have left and center field spoken for in Pittsburgh, and right field projects as a timeshare between Ryan O’Hearn and Esmerlyn Valdez. It’s probably safe to rule the Bucs out on Kwan, though there is a world where the Pirates land the Gold Glover and move Reynolds or Cruz over to right field, thus improving the outfield defense by a large margin.
Rangers: Evan Carter won’t be ready for Opening Day due to a recent hip surgery, plus Carter still hasn’t fully established himself over parts of four MLB seasons. Texas can use Wyatt Langford in either left or center field but Langford is better suited for a corner slot, so bringing Kwan in to handle center field makes a lot of sense.
Rays: The like-minded Guardians and Rays have lined up on several trades in the past, even if Cleveland is still smarting from losing Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz. Tampa Bay might also be moving to move some salaries in order to reload on cheaper and more controllable talent, but the Rays do have a vacancy in center field since Cedric Mullins is unlikely to be re-signed.
Yankees: Between Aaron Judge, Spencer Jones, Cody Bellinger, and Jasson Dominguez, the Bronx outfield is already pretty crowded. The DH spot provides little relief since Giancarlo Stanton is still around, plus Luis Garcia Jr. and Ben Rice will be splitting first base/DH duties if Garcia isn’t given another look at second base. The jury is still out on whether or not Jones can hold his own defensively in center field, so while it’s not out of the question that Kwan could be targeted, the Yankees probably will focus more on their infield needs.

item.title: [ｄメニューニュース] MLB 佐藤輝明＆鈴木誠也、ポジション別FA選手でトップ評価 村上宗隆の移籍「佐藤に追い風」 今永昇太、平良海馬も候補挙がる（SANSPO）｜ｄメニューニュース
item.description: 米大リーグ公式サイトが8日（日本時間9日）、今オフのFA市場でポジション別のトップ選手を特集し、阪神からポスティングシステムを利用してメジャー移籍を目指す佐藤輝明内野手（27）とカブスFAの鈴木誠也外野手（32）が名を連ねた。 佐藤を三塁手のトップに選出した理由として「過去4年で3度85打点以上をマークしたボーム（フィリーズ）を選ぶべきという理由もある。ただ、今回は日本で残した実績を評価した」とし、「村上宗隆（ホワイトソックス）がメジャー移籍後すぐに成功を収めたことも、佐藤にとって追い風になる。村上を上回る契約を目指す上で、その実績は大きな助けになる」と伝えた。 鈴木には「過去4年で安定感の模範ともいえる活躍を続けている。26年は長打力がやや低下したが、打率、出塁率を上昇させ優れた守備力も維持した。送球の強さも上位15％に入った」と攻守で高い評価を受けた。また、カブスFAの今永昇太投手（33）は先発左腕の候補に名前が挙がり、西武からポスティングシステムを利用してメジャー移籍を目指す平良海馬投手（26）は先発右腕の候補に挙がった。

item.content:encoded:
ＭＬＢ公式サイトは７日（日本時間８日）にカブスからＦＡになった鈴木誠也外野手（３２）について「彼はオールスターに選ばれたことはないが、ＦＡの中では最高の打者かもしれない」と絶賛した。カブスから１年契約を求めるクオリファイングオファー（年俸２３１５万ドル＝約３６億７０００万円）を提示されたが、「より長期の契約を結ぶ可能性が高いようだ」とし、大型補強を狙うチームにとっていかに魅力的な存在であるかを検証した。
まずは攻撃の安定性だ。メジャー１年目の２０２２年は１４本塁打、ＯＰＳ０・７７０だったが、、それ以降の４年間は２０本塁打以上、７３打点以上、ＯＰＳ０・８０４以上をマーク、今季の８１四球は移籍後最多だった。
２番目は今オフのＦＡ市場の打者はジャッジ（２２年）、大谷翔平（２３年）、ソト（２４年）、タッカー（２５年）のような大物不在に加え、右の強打者が少ないことだ。ポスティングシステムでメジャー移籍を目指す阪神の佐藤輝明内野手（２７）、チザム（ヤンキースＦＡ）、バウアーズ（ブルワーズＦＡ）、アラエス（フィリーズＦＡ）などは左打者。右の強打者はアロザレーナ（マリナーズＦＡ）くらいだ。「アロザレーナと鈴木は次の契約を探す中で密接に比較されるだろう」という。
３番目は守備力の向上だ。２４年までの３年間は平凡な飛球の落球などがあり、ＦＲＶ（捕球や送球などの守備全体の貢献度）マイナス８で、２５年はタッカーが加入したため、主にＤＨでの起用だった。しかし、今季はＦＲＶ＋７、ＤＲＳ（守備による失点阻止への貢献）はナ・リーグ右翼手トップの＋１４を記録。８補殺は自己最多だった。受賞は逃したがゴールドグラブ賞最終候補３人に残った。守備面は「アロザレーナと比較すると大きな後押しになる可能性がある」とした。
ただ、懸念材料として２点挙げた。打撃でハードヒット率が過去３年間の４８・６パーセントから今季は３８・９パーセントに急落したこと。さらに過去４年間平均以下の守備力だったことから、守備面での改善は本物なのか、考慮すべきとした。
同サイトはＦＡの右翼手部門でトップに鈴木を選出している。

item.content:encoded:
MLB公式サイトが8日（日本時間9日）までに、今FA市場の最注目選手の1人であるカブス・鈴木誠也外野手（32）について、「（MLBの）球宴出場歴なしも、今FA市場で最高の打者の可能性がある」という記事を掲載した。
鈴木は、MLB移籍後の過去5年間で連続2桁本塁打をマークし、同4年間で20本塁打以上を記録している。WBCでの負傷で出遅れた今季も打率．270、26本塁打、86打点、OPS.841の数字を残した。
さらに、今季守備面でも自己最高のFRV（守備貢献度）+7を記録。その総合的な数字が、今FA市場最高の打者へと評価を押し上げている。
そして、カブスは鈴木にクオリファイング・オファー（QO）を提示したが、鈴木自身は長期契約を希望していると紹介。これだけ注目を浴びる選手が、「なぜ球宴に選出されていないの？」との疑問にも触れ、過去の月別成績を一覧とし「シーズンが深まるにつれて成績が上がる傾向にあるため」と結論づけた。

OPS.901
一方で既述のように、守備率も今季は格段に向上。広島時代は、ゴールデングラブ賞を5回受賞。だが、その守備力はMLBですぐには通用しなかった。22年からの3年間では、平凡な飛球を落球し注目を集めるミスもあった。
25年には右翼での出場機会が減り指名打者の出場も増えた。その守備力が今季変化した。持ち前の強肩が磨かれ、外野からの補殺数は自己最多8を記録。FRV（守備貢献度）7、さらにDRS（守備防御点）は14で、ナ・リーグ右翼手の中でトップとなり、受賞は逃したがゴールドグラブ賞の最終候補にもノミネートされた。
FA市場では、右打者ではランディ・アロザレーナ外野手（31、マリナーズ）も注目されている。それでも、この守備力も含めた力で鈴木は「今FA市場、最高の右打者の可能性」と記事は締めている。
予想契約額が、4年総額1億2500万ドル（約197億円）ともされる鈴木。MLB公式サイトで「トップ報道」されるほど、その動向は注目を集めている。

item.title: [Newsday] Predicting the destinations for the top 20 MLB free agents. Where will Tarik Skubal land? - Newsday

item.content:encoded:
History suggests that the next three weeks — leading up to the presumed lockout that would take effect at midnight Dec. 2 — will replicate the free-agent frenzy (to some degree, anyway) from 2021, the last time labor strife effectively shut down baseball.
Five years ago, teams spent more than $2 billion on free agents before the sport went dark, including $1.4 billion spread over 27 new contracts on Dec. 1 alone, a single-day record.
This signing period officially launched Monday at 5 p.m., but the serious discussions — along with potentially the first wave of deals — won’t kick off until the general managers' meetings begin Monday in Las Vegas. From there, the clock will be ticking.
Granted, this year’s free-agent class is extremely top-heavy, with a sizable drop-off after top prize Tarik Skubal, so we don’t expect to see the same eye-popping numbers from 2021. But there is plenty of middle-rotation help, a few impact bats and an A-list closer to tempt owners to dole out some cash even though they won't know the payroll restrictions that await them on the other side of the lockout (if the 2027 season does take place).
Against that backdrop, here is a list of 20 top free agents, along with our predictions for their landing spots. (Fingers crossed we’ll actually get to see them in these new uniforms next summer.)
1. Tarik Skubal
The back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner stands high above the rest of this year’s middling free-agent class, so Skubal shouldn’t have a problem beating Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325 million contract, the current record for a starting pitcher. The fit is too perfect in Flushing, where the owner won't blink at Scott Boras’ demands. Plus there’s no obvious Plan B for missing out on this generational talent.
Prediction: Mets
2. Randy Arozarena
The disappointing Mariners failed to build on their momentum from 2025, but don’t pin that on Arozarena, whose career year should land him in top-10 MVP consideration after he hit .281 with 26 homers, 26 stolen bases and an .865 OPS. Seattle’s qualifying offer might suppress bids, and the defending NL East champs could use the offensive spark.
Prediction: Atlanta
3. Teruaki Sato
Sato can thank the breakout performances of last year’s Japanese free agents — Munetaka Murakami and Kazuma Okamoto — for jacking up his price tag this November. MLB suitors won’t make the same mistake and doubt the offensive transition of the NPB Triple Crown winner (.306 batting average/39 homers/106 RBIs).
Prediction: Mariners
4. Freddy Peralta
Few players, if any, did more to boost their free-agent value after the trade deadline than Peralta, whose stock skyrocketed with the AL champion Rays. Peralta went 5-0 with a 0.79 ERA in his final six regular-season starts, then had a 1.08 ERA in four postseason appearances (three starts) before being dented by Milwaukee in his lone World Series start.
Prediction: Cubs
5. Seiya Suzuki
Suzuki is competing with Arozarena in the corner-outfielder market and has two of the most coveted skills available: He's a dependable righthanded hitter who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense. He batted .270 with 26 homers and an .841 OPS and his 14 defensive runs saved (DRS) ranked eighth among all MLB outfielders. Also has a qualifying offer attached.
Prediction: Blue Jays
6. Michael King
King’s competitive nature was forged in the Bronx, but he further developed his ace-like qualities after arriving in San Diego. He had a 3.15 ERA in three seasons, averaging 26 starts. King polished his resume by allowing one run and striking out 15 in two playoff starts this October. Driving up I-5 makes sense.
Prediction: Dodgers
7. Trevor Rogers
Rogers, who will turn 29 later this month, finally is trending in the right direction again after a shaky three-year stretch plagued by injuries and underperformance. He posted a 1.81 ERA in 2025 in 18 starts, then made 30 for the Orioles last season, pitching better than a 4.03 ERA would suggest (his 1.19 WHIP ranked 13th among AL starters).
Prediction: White Sox
8. Adrian Morejon
Every team dreams of a lefty reliever who throws 100 mph, but only a select few will pony up the cash for one, and Morejon, 27, is going to strike it rich as the most coveted bullpen weapon on the market — or as a starter, as some reports suggest. He’s coming off career highs in appearances (76) and innings (86). He has the qualifying offer attached.
Prediction: Dodgers
9. Brandon Lowe
In a weak position-player class, a second baseman with 35 homers and an .824 OPS should generate plenty of interest. The previously injury-prone Lowe also logged a career-high 150 games in 2026 — funny how that happens in a walk year — but his defense remains a bit of a question mark. The Pirates gave him the qualifying offer.
Prediction: Pirates
10. Luis Arraez
Finding contact-heavy hitters again is the focus after the Brewers won a title by putting the ball in play, and no one does it better than Arraez, a three-time batting champ with the lowest strikeout percentage (5.8) in the majors since 2019. Plays three infield positions but prefers second base, and he has improved there defensively.
Prediction: Tigers
11. David Bednar
Unlike some other imported high-leverage pitchers who flamed out while wearing pinstripes, Bednar checked off the last box as a closer by handling the Bronx pressure. He has a 2.39 ERA and 10.6 K/9 rate in 86 appearances since the 2025 trade deadline. Bednar tied for second in the American League with 35 saves in 2026 and had only four blown chances.
Prediction: Yankees
12. Jake Bauers
After nearly retiring two years ago, Bauers indeed is going to be rich, as Brewers manager Pat Murphy famously told him after the clinching Game 5 of the World Series. It’s just a matter of how rich, as he’s already got the $23.15 million qualifying offer on the table. Bauers hit 26 homers with a 140 OPS+, then was an October hero, further driving up his price tag.
Prediction: Padres
13. Ryan Jeffers
The Yankees had their eye on Jeffers as a trade possibility at the deadline, but the Twins chose to be buyers, and Minnesota extended him the $23.15 million qualifying offer last week. Much of his walk year was derailed by hamate bone surgery, but Jeffers still hit 14 homers and had an .814 OPS in 92 games.
Prediction: Cubs
14. Jazz Chisholm Jr.
Chisholm didn’t quite live up to his bold prediction of a 50-50 season, hitting 19 homers and stealing 41 bases, and unfortunately wound up making more noise with a lollipop than his bat on the way out of the Bronx. Brian Cashman wisely avoided the QO route this time, but the talented Chisholm could regain his groove on a short-term, prove-it deal.
Prediction: Reds
15. Sonny Gray
Gray had a Cy Young Award-caliber season (18-5, 2.72 ERA) with the Red Sox, so even as he turns 37 this month, the 14-year veteran should be a reliable boost to a current contender. Seems like a good match for the defending NL East champs.
Prediction: Atlanta
16. Kevin Gausman
The Blue Jays capitalized on Gausman’s walk-year status at the trade deadline, but at age 35, he’s still got plenty to offer with ace emeritus credentials coming off a combined 32-start season (nine with the Cubs) and a 9.3 K/9 rate. The 14-year vet loved his time in Toronto, so a reunion is a strong possibility.
Prediction: Blue Jays
17. Nick Martinez
Talk about being at the right place at the right time. Martinez already had rejuvenated his post-NPB career before arriving with Tampa Bay this season, but with free agency looming, he went next level, pitching to a 3.10 ERA and 1.09 WHIP and setting career highs in starts (31) and innings (180) for only $13 million. That will be going up significantly, even at age 36.
Prediction: Orioles
18. Clay Holmes
Oh, what might have been this past season for both Holmes and the Mets if not for that 111-mph line drive off the bat of Spencer Jones. Holmes never really got back on track (4.25 ERA) for the Cubs, going straight from Mets rehab to Wrigley in a deadline deal, but this is a story primed for a do-over in Flushing.
Prediction: Mets
19. Shota Imanaga
Imanaga had a good run on the North Side after NPB stardom, with a 3.45 ERA and 1.10 WHIP in three seasons, but the lefty’s penchant for fly balls made him best when the wind was blowing in at Wrigley. He teed up 35 homers this past season, the second-most in the majors, so it’s smart to put him in a spacious, pitcher-friendly home.
Prediction: Giants
20. Kaima Taira
Taira has spent most of his career as a dominant reliever for the Seibu Lions, but he wants to be a full-time starter in MLB and seems to possess the makeup to do so. Having a 100-mph fastball definitely helps, and he’s coming off a 12-5 season with a 1.36 ERA, 0.96 WHIP and 24.8 strikeout percentage in 146 innings.
Prediction: Red Sox

item.title: [MLB.com] ¿Qué tan agresivos deberían ser los Azulejos para reforzar su rotación de cara a 2027?
item.dc:creator: Keegan Matheson
item.description: TORONTO -- Los Azulejos deben estar en la conversación por cualquier agente libre de primer nivel, sin importar su precio. Este invierno, esa lista comienza con Tarik Skubal, uno de los lanzadores más dominantes del deporte. Además del contrato de US$210 millones de Dylan Cease y el megacontrato de US$500 mill
item.content:encoded:
TORONTO -- Los Azulejos deben estar en la conversación por cualquier agente libre de primer nivel, sin importar su precio. Este invierno, esa lista comienza con Tarik Skubal, uno de los lanzadores más dominantes del deporte.
Esta organización está gastando más que nunca, lo suficiente como para sacudirse la etiqueta de «eternos subcampeones» que se les había colocado con cierta ligereza a lo largo de los años. Además del contrato de US$210 millones de Dylan Cease y el megacontrato de US$500 millones de Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Toronto pasó las dos temporadas bajas anteriores apostando fuerte tanto por Shohei Ohtani como por Juan Soto.
Los Azulejos están sentados en la mesa de los grandes, junto a los Dodgers, Filis, Mets, Yankees y algunos otros. Tienen una nómina que les permite pensar que «todo es posible» y han demostrado que están perfectamente dispuestos a pagar por pitcheo, desde Cease hasta Kevin Gausman y José Berríos.
Sin embargo, con necesidades importantes en su alineación, donde Seiya Suzuki parece encajar perfectamente sobre el papel, ¿qué tan agresivos deberían ser los Azulejos con su rotación?
Con qué están trabajando
Si la temporada comenzara mañana, la rotación sería: Dylan Cease, Trey Yesavage, José Soriano, Cody Ponce y posiblemente Spencer Miles, quien se espera que pase del bullpen a la rotación.
Este es un buen punto de partida, pero el grupo necesita un techo más alto y también un piso más sólido, especialmente después de ver el alcance de las lesiones en 2026. Parte de eso también llegará desde adentro, con una lista de prospectos que incluye los siguientes brazos que terminaron 2026 en Doble-A o niveles superiores: Nolan Perry (Nro. 2), Johnny King (Nro. 3), Gage Stanifer (Nro. 9), Jake Bloss (Nro. 11), Danny Thompson Jr. (Nro. 14), Daniel Guerra (Nro. 15), Chad Dallas (Nro. 22) y John Klein (Nro. 29).
Si sumamos a Bowden Francis y Berríos, quienes se están rehabilitando de cirugías Tommy John y podrían regresar más adelante en la temporada, los Azulejos tienen muchas opciones en este departamento. Sin embargo, siguen ansiosos por agregar talento establecido de Grandes Ligas, aunque eso no será barato.
Empezando por lo más alto: Skubal y Peralta
El récord de MLB de salario anual para un lanzador es de US$43.3 millones, cifra que alcanzaron tanto Max Scherzer como Justin Verlander. Skubal está bien posicionado para intentar superar ese número, que se ubica muy por encima de los US$30 millones anuales que los Azulejos le pagan a Cease.
Las finanzas de Toronto lucen bien, algo importante de establecer en este punto. Más allá de Cease y Guerrero, no tienen otros compromisos económicos enormes a largo plazo, y existe la esperanza de que un sistema de granjas mejorado pueda ayudar a proporcionar profundidad de manera más consistente. En términos generales, parece que los Azulejos prefieren mantenerse fieles a contratos más tradicionales, lo que podría traducirse en un acuerdo cercano a los ocho años para Skubal, en lugar de los contratos de corto plazo y grandes sumas de dinero que se han vuelto más populares recientemente.
Se espera que los Azulejos participen en la puja por Skubal, porque a estas alturas eso es prácticamente lo habitual. Tendrá 30 años la próxima temporada, cuenta con dos premios Cy Young y su ERA ha comenzado con un dos en cada una de las últimas cuatro temporadas. Es un verdadero as, de élite bajo cualquier definición de la palabra, pero ¿superarán los Azulejos las ofertas de los Dodgers y los Mets? Un abridor de nivel medio acompañado de mejoras ofensivas más significativas podría ser una alternativa más valiosa.
Freddy Peralta es otro nombre a considerar, recién llegado de disputar la Serie Mundial con los Rays. Hace dos meses, antes de su increíble cierre de temporada, Peralta se perfilaba como un candidato perfecto para recuperar su mejor versión con los Azulejos, gracias a su durabilidad y trayectoria, pero su precio se ha disparado.
Más realista: las opciones de nivel medio
La opción de buscar ofertas económicas no tiene mucho sentido para Toronto, al menos no hasta que lleguen las habituales contrataciones de profundidad más cerca del inicio del campamento. Este equipo todavía debe tener expectativas de llegar a la Serie Mundial y no necesita solamente innings, sino también pitcheo de primer nivel.
El derecho japonés Kaima Taira forma parte de esa lista, especialmente dada la incertidumbre sobre dónde terminará su dinero garantizado y su edad, apenas 27 años, pero el mercado de nivel medio está bien surtido de opciones a corto plazo. Si los Azulejos no hacen una apuesta grande por Skubal, sería prudente que encontraran a «su hombre» entre este grupo con un contrato de dos o tres años, similar al tiempo de Chris Bassitt en Toronto.
Gausman, un viejo conocido, encabeza esa lista, siempre que los Azulejos estén convencidos de que su antiguo as todavía tiene mucho que ofrecer. Tyler Mahle resulta interesante y ya despertó su interés en el pasado. Sonny Gray, Foster Griffin y Shota Imanaga no impresionarán por la velocidad de sus lanzamientos ni por sus tasas de ponches, pero, volviendo al caso de Bassitt, Toronto ya ha mostrado interés en veteranos con repertorios amplios de pitcheos.
El desarrollo de lanzadores de los Azulejos ha dado grandes pasos en los últimos 18 meses, pero eso lleva tiempo, y un veterano con un contrato a corto plazo podría ser el puente perfecto hacia ese objetivo.

item.title: [Swing Completo] Agencia libre MLB: 5 objetivos que podrían cambiar el futuro de Boston Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Guillermo Sanchez
item.description: Boston Red Sox afronta una agencia libre decisiva para fortalecer su plantilla.
