Aunque la organización ha conseguido construir una base
item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox afronta una agencia libre decisiva para fortalecer su plantilla. Craig Breslow tiene cinco alternativas interesantes para potenciar la ofensiva y consolidar la rotación.
Boston necesita convertir su talento joven en resultados concretos. La agencia libre será clave para que Breslow construya un equipo capaz de pelear por el título.
La eliminación en la postemporada volvió a dejar una asignatura pendiente para Boston Red Sox. Aunque la organización ha conseguido construir una base competitiva, el próximo mercado de agentes libres representa una oportunidad para incorporar las piezas que permitan dar un salto definitivo en 2027.
El director de operaciones de béisbol, Craig Breslow, tiene motivos para confiar en el talento disponible. Sin embargo, también sabe que mantener el mismo núcleo no garantiza mejores resultados. La ofensiva fue uno de los principales problemas del equipo durante 2026, especialmente por su limitada producción de extrabases y cuadrangulares.
Los Medias Rojas terminaron en el puesto 23 de MLB en carreras anotadas, con 689, y ocuparon el lugar 26 en jonrones, con apenas 163. El propio Breslow reconoció la necesidad de construir una alineación con mayor capacidad para aprovechar las características particulares de Fenway Park.
En ese escenario, existen cinco nombres que podrían encajar en los planes de Boston. Algunos aportarían poder inmediato, mientras otros ayudarían a fortalecer una rotación que ya cuenta con talento joven y experiencia.
Randy Arozarena: poder, velocidad y personalidad para Fenway Park
Si existe un jugador capaz de aportar energía y producción ofensiva al lineup de Boston, ese es Arozarena. El cubano-mexicano viene de una extraordinaria campaña en la que registró promedio de .281, 26 jonrones, 79 carreras impulsadas, 26 bases robadas y OPS de .865 en 154 encuentros.
Su rendimiento también se reflejó en las métricas avanzadas: acumuló 5.7 de bWAR y 5.5 de fWAR, cifras que lo colocaron entre los jardineros más productivos de la Liga Americana. Además, consiguió su sexta temporada consecutiva con al menos 20 cuadrangulares y 20 estafadas.
Su capacidad para combinar fuerza y velocidad sería especialmente interesante en Fenway Park. Arozarena puede jugar en el jardín izquierdo, una posición que permitiría mantener a Ceddanne Rafaela en el central y a Wilyer Abreu en el derecho.
Hay, sin embargo, un obstáculo económico: Seattle le presentó una oferta calificada de 23.15 millones de dólares para 2027. Si la rechaza y firma con Boston, los Medias Rojas deberán asumir las consecuencias correspondientes en el sistema de compensación del Draft.
Seiya Suzuki: un bate derecho con capacidad para producir extrabases
Boston ya había mostrado interés en Suzuki cuando llegó a MLB desde Japón, pero finalmente fueron los Cubs quienes consiguieron sus servicios. Ahora, después de cinco temporadas en Chicago, vuelve a aparecer como una alternativa interesante para el mercado.
El japonés terminó 2026 con promedio de .270, 26 cuadrangulares, 86 impulsadas y OPS de .841. Su producción estuvo acompañada por 5.1 de bWAR, la mejor cifra de su carrera, además de una evolución defensiva que le permitió registrar números positivos en el jardín derecho.
Su principal atractivo para los Red Sox sería incorporar otro bateador derecho capaz de castigar los lanzamientos hacia los callejones de Fenway. No obstante, su llegada obligaría a resolver el acomodo defensivo, considerando que Abreu es el titular habitual del jardín derecho.
Una alternativa sería utilizarlo como bateador designado y darle oportunidades en los jardines, aunque eso dependería de los movimientos que realice Breslow para reorganizar la plantilla.
Chicago también le presentó una oferta calificada de 23.15 millones de dólares. Por tanto, conseguirlo supondría una inversión importante, tanto salarial como en términos de compensación del Draft.
Sonny Gray: continuidad para una rotación competitiva
En este caso no se trataría de incorporar a un desconocido, sino de intentar conservar una pieza que ya demostró su importancia dentro de la organización.
Gray llegó a Boston después de renunciar a su cláusula de no cambio y respondió con una de las mejores temporadas de su trayectoria. En 29 aperturas consiguió balance de 18-5, efectividad de 2.72 y 169 entradas de trabajo. Sus victorias igualaron la mayor cantidad de MLB durante la campaña.
El derecho rechazó su opción de 30 millones de dólares para 2027, recibió una compensación de 10 millones y quedó disponible en el mercado. No obstante, manifestó disposición para regresar a Boston.
Su continuidad tendría bastante sentido. Garrett Crochet encabezaría una rotación que también cuenta con alternativas como Payton Tolle y Ranger Suárez. Mantener a Gray permitiría conservar experiencia, estabilidad y capacidad para trabajar profundamente en los encuentros.
La edad y el costo serán factores determinantes, pero después de lo demostrado en 2026, sería difícil encontrar argumentos deportivos para descartar una negociación.
Shota Imanaga: una alternativa zurda con experiencia
La conexión entre Imanaga y Breslow viene de tiempo atrás. Cuando el ejecutivo todavía trabajaba en la estructura deportiva de Chicago, siguió de cerca al japonés y respaldó su incorporación a los Cubs.
El zurdo acumula tres temporadas en Grandes Ligas con efectividad de 3.45 en 86 aperturas. Durante 2026 trabajó 174.1 entradas, consiguió 174 ponches y terminó con balance de 11-10 y promedio de carreras limpias de 3.77.
Aunque sus números no fueron tan dominantes como los de su campaña de estreno, demostró que puede ofrecer volumen de trabajo y mantener una rotación estable.
Para Boston sería una incorporación interesante por su capacidad para atacar a los bateadores desde distintos ángulos y complementar a Crochet, Gray y los brazos jóvenes de la organización.
Su principal interrogante estaría relacionado con la consistencia y el costo de un contrato multianual. Aun así, Breslow conoce perfectamente sus características y tendría argumentos para apostar nuevamente por él.
Kaima Taira: una apuesta internacional con potencial
La alternativa más diferente de esta lista es Taira, quien acaba de recibir autorización para negociar con organizaciones de MLB mediante el sistema de posting de la liga japonesa.
El derecho viene de una campaña extraordinaria en Japón. Después de desempeñarse principalmente como relevista, regresó a la rotación de los Seibu Lions en 2026 y registró efectividad de 1.36 y WHIP de 0.96 en 23 presentaciones. En su trayectoria de ocho temporadas en la NPB acumula promedio de carreras limpias de 1.78 y 9.4 ponches por cada nueve entradas.
Su principal atractivo es la versatilidad. Taira tiene experiencia como abridor y relevista, mientras que su repertorio y capacidad para generar ponches podrían ofrecerle a Boston diferentes alternativas de utilización.
Con apenas 26 años, representa una inversión con mayor proyección que las otras opciones de esta lista. Además, al superar los 25 años, no estaría sujeto a las restricciones contractuales que afectan a determinados jugadores internacionales más jóvenes.
Boston tendría 45 días para negociar con él desde su incorporación al sistema de posting. Una oportunidad que Breslow podría aprovechar para incorporar talento internacional sin depender exclusivamente del mercado tradicional.
Japanese RHP Kaima Taira of the Saitama Seibu Lions (NPB) has entered MLB’s posting system. In 2026, he went 12-5 with a 1.36 ERA and 141 Ks in 146 innings. Taira, who turns 27 on November 15, holds a career 1.78 ERA across eight NPB seasons. https://t.co/7veoJKdCUL— MLB (@MLB)
November 2, 2026

¿Cuál debería ser la prioridad de Boston?
Los cinco nombres presentan características diferentes, pero todos responden a necesidades que Boston debe atender si pretende competir por algo más que una clasificación a la postemporada.
Arozarena y Suzuki representan soluciones ofensivas para una alineación que necesita más poder derecho. Gray e Imanaga aportarían profundidad y experiencia a una rotación con buenos argumentos para convertirse en una de las fortalezas del equipo. Taira, por su parte, sería una apuesta de desarrollo y versatilidad.
La prioridad, sin embargo, debería estar en conseguir un bateador de impacto. Boston tiene suficiente talento joven para construir alrededor de su núcleo actual, pero necesita transformar esa capacidad de embasarse en carreras y cuadrangulares.
Breslow tiene una decisión importante por delante: conformarse con mantener la estructura competitiva o invertir para convertir a los Red Sox en verdaderos aspirantes al título de la División Este de la Liga Americana.

item.content:encoded:
Skip to content
Trade season is upon us. Here are potential targets for the Phillies to address their big needs.
As baseball descends on Las Vegas for the GM meetings Monday, the trade market might be stimulated by the compressed offseason. Let's look at four players who could be fits with the Phillies.
Executives from 30 major league front offices will walk into a Las Vegas resort and casino Monday evening for the annual general managers’ meetings.
That’s a lot of poker faces.
But with the owners poised to lock out the players upon the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, the meetings could serve as the launching pad for a three-week free-agent frenzy.
That’s how it happened five years ago. With baseball barreling toward a labor fight, teams spent a total of nearly $2 billion on free agents in the weeks before the owners locked out the players.
» READ MORE: A (likely long) lockout looms again for MLB. Why a salary cap is at the center of it all. Again.
Tarik Skubal is easily the headliner of this free-agent class, but if the two-time Cy Young Award winner signs before the lockout, he won’t be alone. Fellow starting pitchers Michael King, Freddy Peralta, and Clay Holmes, and relievers Adrian Morejon and David Bednar could come off the board, too.
The Phillies are interested in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, multiple sources confirmed, likely as a left fielder even though he played mostly third base in Japan. But two non-Phillies talent evaluators said they graded him as a below-average defender at every position.
Sato, who turns 28 in March, also bats left-handed. Coupled with the defensive questions, that could leave the Phillies to favor a pair of righty-hitting outfielders entering their age-32 seasons with nearly identical five-year numbers, including batting average/on-base/slugging slash lines and Fangraphs’ WAR:
- Seiya Suzuki: .269/.351/.472, 113 homers, 24.8% strikeout rate, 128 OPS+, 15.6 WAR in 675 games
- Randy Arozarena: .251/.348/.434, 116 homers, 24.6% strikeout rate, 124 OPS+, 16.2 WAR in 772 games
Suzuki and Arozarena are likely in line for similar four- or five-year contracts. And because both received the free-agent qualifying offer, signing them would involve draft-pick compensation. But either player would boost a Phillies lineup that this season was 26th in OPS from outfielders (.686), 29th from the cleanup spot (.645), and 30th from the right side of the plate (.658).
The Phillies have other needs, too, and with roughly $280 million in luxury-tax commitments for 2027, president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski won’t be able to throw money at all of them.
It’s possible the trade market will also be stimulated by the compressed offseason calendar, officials from multiple clubs suggested this week.
The GM meetings are usually a time when teams lay the groundwork for activity later in the offseason. But with limited time to make deals, and every front office under one roof for two days this week, it could be fertile ground for accelerated trade talks.
(History lesson: The Phillies famously traded for closer Brad Lidge at the GM meetings in 2007.)
Let’s focus on four players who may be available for various reasons and would potentially fit the Phillies’ roster:
Steven Kwan
A few days before the trade deadline in 2025, the Guardians were under .500 and reeling from the news that star closer Emmanuel Clase would be out indefinitely as the subject of an investigation into his involvement in a sports-betting scheme.
So, they began listening to offers for Kwan.
The Phillies tried to trade for the All-Star left fielder, major league sources said at the time. But with Kwan under club control through 2027, Cleveland kept him and was rewarded with a late surge to the AL Central title — and another division crown this year. (The Phillies instead acquired center fielder Harrison Bader from the Twins.)
» READ MORE: Will the Phillies spend to beef up the middle of the order? Here are some free-agent options.
Rival team officials believe Kwan may be available again given the low-payroll Guardians’ history of trading stars as they enter their last year before free agency. They dealt Corey Kluber after the 2019 season, Francisco Lindor in January 2021, and Josh Naylor three years later. It’s how the Guardians remain competitive — and they’ve made the playoffs in eight of 11 seasons.
If Kwan, projected to make $11.3 million next year, is next to go, the Phillies should remain interested.
The 29-year-old is a contact-hitting, on-base machine who has reached base at a .357 clip, including a career-best .382 mark this season, with a 9.5% strikeout rate. He’s cut from a similar mold as Luis Arraez with two notable differences: He swings less than Arraez and walks almost twice as often. Like Arraez, Kwan would be a counterweight to the Phillies’ swing-and-miss tendencies.
Kwan is also a four-time Gold Glove-winning left fielder and above average in center. The Phillies could reimagine the outfield by signing Suzuki or Arozarena, trading for Kwan, giving Justin Crawford the majority of the at-bats in center field, and trading Brandon Marsh for a reliever or backup catcher.
The Guardians were reportedly believed to be seeking top-100 prospects for Kwan in 2025. With only one year of control, the return figures to be lower now. Start here: Change-of-scenery-candidate reliever Orion Kerkering and a couple of positional prospects from among Aroon Escobar, Bryan Rincon, Dante Nori, and Gabriel Rincones Jr.
Isaac Paredes
A year ago, the Astros reportedly discussed swapping Paredes for Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran. It didn’t materialize, and they went into the season with an infield surplus that came in handy when third baseman Carlos Correa tore an ankle tendon in May.
But Correa is expected to be healthy to begin next season, leaving new general manager Randy Flores with a familiar problem: Too many infielders.
The Astros exercised Paredes’ $13.35 million option but could still choose to unload him (or shortstop Jeremy Peña, also entering his walk year) and add to another area of the roster.
» READ MORE: With help from TB12, Aidan Miller is healthy, grateful for adversity, and primed to impact the Phillies in 2027
Paredes, 27, has right-handed power with 115 homers over the last five seasons, including 25 this year. He’s also patient at the plate (11% career walk rate) and tends to put the ball in play, making him a fit to bat behind Bryce Harper. He would slot in at third base, replacing free agent Alec Bohm and facilitating Bryson Stott’s return to second.
One potential complication: Trading for Paredes could block top prospect Aidan Miller — unless Trea Turner moves to the outfield.
(Worth noting: In discussing a position change for Turner, Dombrowski said last month that the $300 million shortstop “prefers the infield.”)
In any case, it’s not clear that the Phillies and Astros would match up in a trade. Houston owner Jim Crane has little tolerance for rebuilding, and the Astros are reportedly seeking starting pitching and outfielders.
Jordan Hicks
For a bullpen that ranked 21st in the majors in ERA, the seats are filling up quickly alongside Phillies star closer Jhoan Duran.
Right-handers Alex McFarlane, Jonathan Bowlan, and Caleb Kilian are ticketed for spots. The Phillies re-signed lefty Tim Mayza after the season and will add a high-leverage lefty to replace José Alvarado. (Free-agent options include Morejon and Alex Vesia.) And they could collect a handful of optionable relievers to fill the final two spots.
But setup man Brad Keller, last offseason’s big bullpen addition, is expected to miss all or most of 2027 after Tommy John elbow surgery. It’s fair to wonder if McFarlane (19 major league appearances) and Kilian (57) are sufficient replacements for Keller and likely Kerkering, whose second-half struggles landed him back in triple A and firmly on the trade market.
The Phillies went after Hicks in free agency three years ago but were rebuffed when he accepted the Giants’ offers of four years, $44 million, and a chance to start. He bounced from starting back to relieving — and from San Francisco to Boston to Chicago — before winding up as a veteran in the upstart White Sox’s young bullpen. He will make $12 million in the last year of his contract.
At age 30, Hicks still throws as hard as ever (average fastball velocity: 99.2 mph). Phillies pitching coach Caleb Cotham loves a good sweeper, and Hicks’ is a weapon against right-handed hitters (.161 opposing batting average). Cotham’s challenge would be to rein in a walk rate that ballooned to 15.3%.
But the electric stuff might be worth the dice roll.
Freddy Fermin
Ethan Salas, who made his major league debut Sept. 2 and won’t turn 21 until next June, was behind the plate for three of the Padres’ postseason games. The other three were started by Luis Campusano.
Where does that leave Freddy Fermin?
The Phillies are looking for a more capable backup to help lighten J.T. Realmuto’s league-leading workload. Defense is a high priority, according to Dombrowski, especially because the bar is low to match the combined .316 OPS from Rafael Marchán and Garrett Stubbs. The Phillies outrighted Stubbs last week.
» READ MORE: What the World Series teams and one stellar August can show the Phillies about improving in 2027
Fermin, 31, led Padres catchers with 74 starts in the regular season but slipped to third-string on the depth chart after batting .203 with a .589 OPS. He’s a better hitter (.251 career average, .665 OPS), though his strength is his defense.
Since 2023, Fermin is tied for second among all catchers in defensive runs saved (45) and eighth in fielding run value. He gets high marks for blocking and pop time on throws to second base.
“We do emphasize defense more in our catching position than we do offense,” Dombrowski said. “And a lot of times, if you’re talking about having somebody who can hit and be a good defensive person, it’d be probably an everyday catcher somewhere because they’re not that easy to find.”
Fermin might fit the description.

item.content:encoded:
【ロサンゼルス=共同】米大リーグで打撃のベストナインに相当するシルバースラッガー賞の最終候補が5日、発表され、ナ・リーグは指名打者（DH）部門にドジャースの大谷翔平、外野手部門にカブスでプレーした鈴木誠也が入った。選出されれば大谷はア・リーグのエンゼルス時代から4年連続5度目、鈴木は初となる。受賞者は17日に発表される。
DH部門は、打率2割7分5厘、30本塁打、81打点の大谷と45本塁打で本塁打王のシュワバー（フィリーズ）が争う。外野手部門には、打率2割7分、26本塁打、86打点の鈴木とカブスのクローアームストロングら7人が名を連ねた。
同賞は各球団の監督とコーチの投票で、各ポジションから選ばれる。ともにメジャー1年目で30本塁打以上を放ったホワイトソックスの村上宗隆とブルージェイズの岡本和真は、ア・リーグの最終候補から漏れた。

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees’ Ben Rice, Cody Bellinger named finalists for AL Silver Slugger Award
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger were officially announced as American League Silver Slugger Award finalists. Award creator and sponsor Louisville Slugger announced the finalists on Thursday morning, with the winners to be revealed on November 17th. item.content:encoded:
Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger were officially announced as American League Silver Slugger Award finalists. Award creator and sponsor Louisville Slugger announced the finalists on Thursday morning, with the winners to be revealed on November 17th.
The Silver Slugger Award was created in 1980 to recognize the best hitter at each position in their respective leagues, with the award recently expanded to be given to a utility player as well as one for the best offensive team in each league. Unlike many of the other year-end honors including MVP, Cy Young, and Rookie of the Year, the Silver Slugger is not decided by the BBWAA. Instead, coaches and managers from each team cast votes for the winner and are not allowed to vote for players on their own teams.
This is Ben Rice's second straight appearance as a finalist for the award, getting nominated in the utility category last year before losing out to Zach McKinstry of the Tigers. Despite splitting reps between first base and DH, Rice earns the nod in the DH category this year. Rice led all Yankees position players with 4.2 fWAR this season, finishing third in MLB in slugging (.534) fifth in wRC+ (149) and seventh in home runs (41). Overall, he slashed .264/.363/.534 while also adding a team-high 105 runs and 97 RBIs in 154 games. Should he win, this would be Rice's first major award of his career — but given his competition, he's probably a long shot.
As for Bellinger, this is also his second straight nomination as a finalist for the award, missing out last year to Aaron Judge, Byron Buxton, and Riley Greene. Bellinger has already secured two pieces of hardware this offseason, winning the AL Gold Glove Award and the Fielding Bible Award in left field. Despite missing a month to a hamstring injury, Bellinger still finished third among left fielders with 3.5 fWAR and fifth in wRC+ (115). In 121 games, Bellinger slashed .264/.338/.429 with 17 home runs, 73 runs scored, and 73 RBIs. Should Bellinger be voted winner on November 17th, it would be the third Silver Slugger award of his career, the other two coming in 2019 and 2023.
As for the rest of the AL nominees, Dillon Dingler and Carter Jensen are finalists at catcher. Pete Alonso and Willson Contreras are first base finalists after both finished in the top-six in MLB in wRC+. Kody Clemens and Chase Meidroth are the second base finalists. Finalists at short include AL MVP finalist Bobby Witt Jr., likely AL Rookie of the Year Kevin McGonigle, and Zach Neto. At third base is AL MVP finalist Junior Caminero and Miguel Vargas, the pair finishing tied for 12th in MLB in fWAR.
The outfield finalists joining Bellinger are Mike Trout, Wilyer Abreu, Randy Arozarena, Chase DeLauter, Jac Caglianone, Chandler Simpson, Riley Greene, and Tristan Peters. It's a tight group and Bellinger might well end up outside the top three. Rice also has tough competition at DH with likely AL MVP Yordan Alvarez named as the other finalist. Rounding out the finalists are McGonigle, Sam Antonacci, and Ezequiel Duran at utility, while the Astros, Rays, Twins, and White Sox are your team finalists.
Over on the NL side of the award, Hunter Goodman and Gabriel Moreno are finalists at catcher. NLCS MVP and World Series winner Jake Bauers is joined by Alec Burleson, Rafael Devers, and Matt Olson as first base finalists. NL MVP finalist Brice Turang and Brandon Lowe are finalists at second base. Elly De La Cruz was snubbed as an NL MVP finalist, but is nominated for this award alongside CJ Abrams and Otto Lopez at shortstop. Alex Bregman and Max Muncy are your third base finalists.
In the outfield, presumptive NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong leads the way, accompanied by Jackson Chourio, Corbin Carroll, Seiya Suzuki, Fernando Tatis Jr., James Wood, and Jordan Walker. NL MVP finalist Shohei Ohtani is joined by Kyle Schwarber as DH finalists. Finally, Bauers and Tatis are joined by NL Rookie of the Year finalist Sal Stewart in the utility category while the Brewers, Cubs, Dodgers, and Nationals are your team finalists.
Best of luck to Ben and Cody!

item.content:encoded:
3 Best MLB Free Agent Fits For Seiya Suzuki If He Leaves Cubs
Power. Lots and lots of power.
That's what one is getting if they sign Chicago Cubs right fielder and designated hitter Seiya Suzuki, who's arguably the biggest power threat on the MLB free agent market this winter. Plus, the 32-year-old Suzuki is coming off quite possibly the best all-around season of his MLB career, offering both a respectable defensive presence in right field and a potent threat from the right side of the plate.
Here are the three best MLB free agent fits for Suzuki should he depart Chicago:
Simply put: The Cincinnati Reds need a right fielder.
The Reds continue to struggle to get consistent production from their outfield and offense as a whole. Plus, the Eugenio Suárez reunion didn't live up to the hype in 2026, as he finished with a mere .212/.307/.433 slash line while splitting time at the hot corner and designated hitter, and is now a free agent.
Suzuki would presumably become Cincinnati's starting right fielder, adding veteran assurance and an impactful veteran complement. Suzuki's electric bat would boost a Reds' offense that was last in MLB in hits (1,231) and on-base percentage (.305), 27th in runs (666) and 25th in slugging percentage (.394) last season.
Prior to 2026, Suzuki was Chicago's primary designated hitter in 2025 before making 110 starts and 111 appearances altogether in right field last season. On that front, Suzuki posted a career-high 5.1 wins above replacement while also logging 14 defensive runs.
Now, Cincinnati may want Héctor Rodríguez to be its everyday right fielder. In that case, Suzuki opens the season as the Reds' designated hitter and moves to right field if Rodríguez struggles or injury presents itself. While the Reds were fourth in the sport with 213 home runs last season, they need the offense, and Suzuki would provide a major lift in that regard.
What could stop the Reds — who finished in last place in the National League Central with 75 wins last season — from making a push for Suzuki, though, is them potentially feeling they're not close enough to contending for the playoffs to be doling out a potential nine-figure contract. Rather, they may hope that Rodríguez emerges as a building block and be cost-effective in filling out the rest of their depth chart.
The Texas Rangers need some oomph, which is precisely what Suzuki would provide.
Just one year ago in 2025, Suzuki, who boasts a career .472 slugging percentage and a 128 OPS+, totaled 32 home runs and 103 RBIs, both career highs. Suzuki would enhance a Texas offense that was just 25th in runs (673), 23rd in hits (1,296) and tied for 21st in slugging percentage (.396) last season.
As for Suzuki's potential fit with the Rangers, designated hitter Joc Pederson is a free agent, which would be the easiest way to slide Suzuki into the mix. Concurrently, right fielder Brandon Nimmo has the versatility and experience playing all three outfield positions should Texas want to play Suzuki in right field.
While Evan Carter is a commendable center fielder, he continues to struggle at the plate (Carter hit .194 across 455 plate appearances in 2026), creating a scenario where Texas could either move Wyatt Langford from left to center field or put Nimmo in center field, with Suzuki taking over in right field.
Either way, the Rangers — who, aside from Langford, have been unable to get their touted young position players to progress as hitters — need more slugging, and they have the wiggle room to add to their outfield rotation.
The Houston Astros won the American League West with a .500 record, edging out the Rangers by one game. It's reasonable to think the Rangers' starting rotation — a unit that led MLB with a 3.41 ERA in 2025 — will bounce back in 2027. With that in mind, a slightly improved offense could literally be all they need to win the AL West.
All that said, Texas may prefer to retain Pederson, who hit 26 home runs and posted a .487 slugging percentage in 2026, on a short-term deal to be its designated hitter and avoid switching gears with who plays where in the outfield.
At face value, the Atlanta Braves don't have a burning need for a right fielder. When putting a magnifying glass closer to the object at hand, though, signing Suzuki would be a slick move.
For starters, the Braves were muzzled by the Los Angeles Dodgers — who were then swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Championship Series — in the NL Division Series, tallying just eight runs and 18 hits across the would-be four-game series. Meanwhile, versatile left fielder Mauricio Dubón, outfielder and midseason pickup Lane Thomas and designated hitter/first baseman Dominic Smith are free agents.
Adding a considerable hitter who's also a body for the outfield mix would be timely.
Suzuki represents a defensive alternative to Ronald Acuña Jr., who has underwhelmed at the corner outfield position by his standards of late and made 14 starts as the team's designated hitter last season, and offers a way for the Braves to ease the homegrown star into being the team's DH on a more consistent basis, if wanted.
Plus, the combination of a torn ACL, as well as calf and hamstring issues, have limited Acuña to just 251 regular games since the outset of the 2023 MLB season. Adding another All-Star-caliber outfielder to the mix warrants consideration from a health standpoint, alone.
Suzuki would fit Atlanta's timeline as an NL contender with a core of players who are primarily in their prime.

item.content:encoded:
「おそらく最高の野手」鈴木誠也にカブスがQO提示！ 拒否が濃厚で去就に注目「受諾したのはわずか18人」
2026.11.4 07:02 NEW
Getty Images
鈴木誠也 最新情報
　シカゴ・カブスに所属する32歳の鈴木誠也外野手に対し、同球団が1年総額2315万ドル（約36億6000万円）のクオリファイング・オファー（QO）を提示した。同選手はこのオファーを拒否する見通しだと、米メディア『NBCスポーツ』が報じている。
QOは、フリーエージェント（FA）となる選手に球団が提示する1年契約のオファーである。
選手が拒否して他球団と契約した場合、元の球団はドラフト指名権の補償を受けられる仕組みだ。
同メディアのジョージ・ビッセル記者は、鈴木について「今オフのFA市場において、おそらく最高の野手」と評価している。
ただ、2012年にQO制度が始まって以降、提示を受けた157人のうち「受諾したのはわずか18人」にとどまるようだ。
2026年シーズンの鈴木は、545打席で打率.270、出塁率.368、長打率.473、26本塁打、86打点、96得点を記録。
2022年にカブスへ加入してから5シーズンのうち4シーズンで20本塁打以上をマークしており、同メディアは安定した長打力の持ち主として鈴木を評している。
 
一方、カブスはイアン・ハップ外野手とマシュー・ボイド投手にはQOを提示しなかった。
同メディアはこの判断について「注目に値する」と伝えている。
鈴木の評価は他のメディアでも高い。
米公式サイト『MLB.com』のマーク・フェインサンド記者が選んだFA選手トップ30では、鈴木は全体5位にランクインしている。
ただし、打球の質には陰りも見える。
同メディアは、鈴木のハードヒット率が2023〜2025年の48.6％から、2026年は38.9％に低下したと指摘している。
8月に32歳を迎えた鈴木が、今オフの野手市場の目玉として、どの球団と契約を結ぶのか注目が集まりそうだ。

item.content:encoded:
大物FAがひしめく今オフのMLB市場で、日本人選手が補強の切り札として脚光を浴びている。中でも阪神からポスティングシステムでメジャー移籍を目指す佐藤輝明内野手（27）をめぐっては、名門同士の宿敵対決が勃発する可能性がありそうだ。
米有力紙「ニューヨーク・タイムズ」傘下のスポーツ専門サイト「ジ・アスレチック」は3日（現地時間）、レッズとナショナルズでGMを務めたジム・ボウデン氏による全30球団の今冬の補強課題を特集。同氏が各球団のフロントに聞き取りを行い、日本人選手を補強候補とみる球団の顔ぶれを分析した。
まず佐藤だ。今季打率3割6厘、39本塁打、106打点で3冠王に輝いた左の大砲には複数の需要がある。レッドソックスは打線の強化を最優先課題に掲げ、三塁を守れる佐藤が補強ポイントに合致するとみている。ヤンキースについても、ボウデン氏は内野陣の再編に絡めて獲得を提言。打線の中軸を担う新たな強打者として期待を寄せる。右打ちの長距離砲を探すマリナーズも、左打ちの佐藤を候補の一人に挙げた。東西の人気球団が争奪戦を演じても不思議ではない。
一方、カブスからFAとなった鈴木誠也外野手（32）は、2日（同3日）に古巣からクオリファイング・オファー（QO）を提示されたが、他球団からも熱視線を浴びそうだ。今季26本塁打、86打点をマークした右の強打者に対し、外野強化が急務のオリオールズには適任と評価。フィリーズも最優先補強ポイントの外野で、鈴木とマリナーズからFAとなったランディ・アロザレーナを有力な選択肢に据える。打線の立て直しを図るブルージェイズも獲得に動くと予測され、マリナーズも候補に加わる。4球団の思惑が交錯する構図だ。
同じくカブスからFAとなった今永昇太投手（33）には、先発陣の強化を急ぐブレーブスが浮上した。今季11勝を挙げた左腕は、大物先発のトレード獲得が実現しない場合、マイケル・キングやソニー・グレイらと並んで獲得を検討する候補という。
12月1日（同2日）の労使協定失効とロックアウトの懸念が迫る中、日本人選手をめぐる争奪戦も時間との勝負になりそうだ。
東スポWEB

item.title: [NBC New York] 8 MLB players received qualifying offers. What does that mean for free agency?
item.dc:creator: Ronald Blum; The Associated Press
item.description: New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams Monday. Milwaukee Brewers first baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers and Baltimore Orioles left-hander Trevor Rogers also received the offers, along with Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe and San Diego Padres left-hander Adrian Morejon. Players
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams Monday.
Milwaukee Brewers first baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers and Baltimore Orioles left-hander Trevor Rogers also received the offers, along with Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe and San Diego Padres left-hander Adrian Morejon.
Players have until Nov. 17 to accept.
Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season, and only 18 of 157 prior offers have been accepted. The figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts this year.
A free agent can be made a qualifying offer only if he has been with the same team continuously since opening day and has never received a qualifying offer before.
If a team makes a qualifying offer to a player who signs a major league contract with another club before the next amateur draft, his former club receives draft pick compensation at the end of the first round or at the end of competitive balance round B. The placement depends on the amount of the new contract and the revenue-sharing and luxury tax status of the team losing the player.
Among those not receiving an offer was Philadelphia Phillies third baseman Alex Bohm.
Twenty-eight more players became free agents, raising the total to 183. Players could start negotiating terms with all teams at 5 p.m. ET on Monday.
Major League Baseball is expected to impose a lockout when the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, likely creating a signing frenzy in the run-up.
Option and opt-out decisions
Baltimore declined a $7.5 million option on first baseman Ryan Mountcastle, limited to eight games this year by a broken left foot sustained when he stumbled while on the basepaths on April 8. The Orioles turned down a $3.5 million option on left-hander Dietrich Enns, which called for a $125,000 buyout.
Corbin Burnes decided not to opt out of the final four seasons of his $210 million, six-year contract with the Arizona Diamondbacks. The deal calls for $35 million annual salaries, including $11 million deferred each year. The 32-year-old right-hander returned to the major leagues on Sept. 8 after a 15-month recovery from Tommy John surgery, made three starts and went back on the injured list because of shoulder inflammation.
Toronto Blue Jays right-hander José Berríos decided not to opt out of the final two seasons of his $131 million, seven-year contract, which call for salaries of $24 million per season. The 32-year-old did not pitch this year and is recovering from Tommy John surgery on May 20.
Athletics right-hander Luis Severino exercised a $22 million player option for 2027, the last season of a $67 million, three-year contract agreed to in December 2025. The 32-year-old was 2-6 with a 4.16 ERA in 12 starts, not pitching after May 29 because of a strained right shoulder.
Baltimore reliever Ryan Helsley did not opt out of his $14 million salary next season, part of a $28 million, two-year contract. The 32-year-old right-hander was 0-4 with a 4.11 ERA and eight saves in 17 relief appearances. He didn’t pitch for the Orioles between April 28 and June 17 because of right elbow inflammation, returned for five outings and then went back on the IL with elbow discomfort. He did not pitch again this season.
Houston Astros right-hander Tatsuya Imai did not opt out of the final two seasons of a $54 million, three-year contract, which calls for salaries of $18 million in 2027 and 2028. Imai also has the right to opt out after next season. The 28-year-old was 6-4 with a 4.93 ERA in 15 starts and eight relief appearances.
Cubs right-handers Clay Holmes, Hunter Harvey and Colin Rea became free agents along with left-hander Caleb Thielbar after their 2027 options were declined, while righty Jacob Webb agreed to a $2.5 million, one-year contract.
Arizona right-hander Michael Soroka declined his $10 million mutual option for 2027, triggering a $1 million buyout. Soroka, 29, was 9-5 with a 3.41 ERA in 21 starts and one relief appearance after signing a one-year contract that guaranteed $7.5 million. He earned $1.35 million in performance bonuses. He was sidelined between June 19 and Aug. 10 by a left glute strain.
Cleveland declined right-hander Shawn Armstrong’s $8 million mutual option in favor of a $1.5 million buyout. The 36-year-old had a one-year deal guaranteeing $5.5 million and went 2-1 with a 4.58 ERA in 41 relief appearances. He was out between July 24 and Sept. 23 because of a strained left calf.
World Series champion Milwaukee declined an $8.5 million mutual option on catcher Gary Sánchez, who gets a $250,000 buyout as part of a one-year contract guaranteeing $1.75 million. The Brewers also turned down a $14 million option on right-hander Antonio Senzatela, part of a $50.5 million, five-year contract he agreed to with Colorado.
Detroit declined a $12 million option on reliever Kenley Jansen. The 39-year-old right-hander, third on the career list with 498 saves, gets a $2 million buyout as part of an $11 million, one-year contract. The Tigers exercised a $10 million option on right-hander Drew Anderson, who had a $7 million salary this year.
Toronto declined an $8 million option on outfielder Myles Straw, who gets a $1.75 million buyout that completes a $25 million, five-year contract he signed with Cleveland.
St. Louis declined a $6 million option on right-hander Ryne Stanek, who gets a $1 million buyout as part of a contract guaranteeing $3.5 million.
Tampa Bay’s Yandy Díaz’s option vested at $13 million after the Rays deemed him healthy for 2027. Díaz reached the 500 plate appearances needed for the option to become guaranteed and had to meet the second provision.
Arbitration-eligible players
Among players who would have been eligible for arbitration if their options had been declined, Milwaukee exercised catcher William Contreras, the World Series MVP, at $14.5 million; Tampa Bay exercised Gold Glove shortstop Taylor Walls at $3.1 million; and Houston exercised infielder Isaac Paredes at $13.35 million.
San Francisco declined an $800,000 option on right-hander Rowan Wick, who gets a $100,000 buyout. If tendered a 2027 contract, he would be eligible for arbitration.
Detroit agreed to a $1.3 million, one-year contract with right-hander Jacob Waguespack, who can earn $300,000 in performance bonuses based on innings; $25,000 each for 45 and 50, and $50,000 apiece for 55, 60 and 65.
Once-touted prospect on the market
Baltimore outfielder Heston Kjerstad became a minor league free agent after clearing waivers. Kjerstad was the No. 2 pick in the 2020 draft and has played 117 games across four seasons in the majors.
Baltimore outfielder Leody Taveras cleared waivers and elected free agency.

item.title: [Chicago Sun-Times] Pete Crow-Armstrong, Alex Bregman win Gold Glove Awards, backing Cubs' reputation as baseball's best defense
item.dc:creator: Vinnie Duber
item.description: The Cubs had baseball’s best defense in 2026, and it wasn’t even close. Now, they’ve got the hardware to prove it. Center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won Gold Gloves when the annual position-by-position defensive awards were announced Sunday night. item.content:encoded:
The Cubs had baseball’s best defense in 2026, and it wasn’t even close.
Now, they’ve got the hardware to prove it.
Center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won Gold Gloves when the annual position-by-position defensive awards were announced Sunday night.
Three other Cubs – shortstop Dansby Swanson, left fielder Ian Happ and right fielder Seiya Suzuki – were previously announced as finalists at their respective positions but did not win.
Still, between the winners and the near-winners, the team’s reputation as the sport’s finest in the field was backed up in a big way.
The statistics did that plenty prior to Sunday’s haul, with the Cubs boasting massive leads in defensive metrics like Outs Above Average (73, compared to the 44 of the second-place Diamondbacks), Defensive Runs Saved (115, compared to the 87 of the second-place Rays) and Fielding Run Value (72, compared to the 46 mark of the second-place Blue Jays).
So whether you prefer numbers or trophies, there was no question: The Cubs were baseball’s best defensive team.
The eye test, if that’s your thing, did a lot to seal that argument, too, and the Cubs spent the summer making one fantastic play after another, talking often about defense as the backbone of a team built to contend for a championship.
That championship, of course, never came, and as good as the gloves were, they did little to stave off postseason embarrassment. The Cubs stumbled in the regular season’s final week, failing to secure home-field advantage in the wild-card round, and were swept without putting up too much fight in just two games against the Padres.
That finish might dominate the memory of fans, but they watched an otherwise thrilling summer at Wrigley Field – and the defense had a lot to do with that.
Crow-Armstrong, who’s expected to win the NL MVP, made defense a cornerstone of his case for the sport’s top individual award, with his excellence in the field and at the plate compared to the two-way dominance of Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani, creating a meaty debate prior to late-season health issues that took Ohtani out of the race.
Crow-Armstrong’s defensive exploits helped him to a jaw-dropping 10.6 fWAR that dwarfed that of all other position players in the game. This Gold Glove was his second in as many seasons.
Bregman, now a two-time Gold Glover, isn’t going anywhere after the Cubs locked him up last offseason, and that’s great news for them after the 32-year-old posted perhaps the best defensive season of his career at the hot corner. His 15 Defensive Runs Saved nearly doubled his previous career high, and he set a new career high with eight Outs Above Average, as well.
Bregman became the Cubs’ first Gold Glover at third base since Ron Santo in 1968.

2022年に新設されたユーティリティ部門のみ、監督・コーチによる投票の対象外となり、この部門に関しては特別に設計された守備指標を用いて選出されることになっている。

ユーティリティ：エゼキエル・デュラン（レンジャーズ）　初受賞
ナ・リーグ
投手：ノーラン・マクレーン（メッツ）　初受賞
捕手：ガブリエル・モレノ（ダイヤモンドバックス）　3年ぶり2度目

二塁手：ブライス・トゥラング（ブルワーズ）　2年ぶり2度目
三塁手：アレックス・ブレグマン（カブス）　2年ぶり2度目
遊撃手：ヘラルド・ペルドモ（ダイヤモンドバックス）　初受賞
左翼手：ジャクソン・チューリオ（ブルワーズ）　初受賞
中堅手：ピート・クロウ＝アームストロング（カブス）　2年連続2度目
右翼手：コービン・キャロル（ダイヤモンドバックス）　初受賞

item.title: [Chicago Tribune] Chicago Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman win Gold Glove Awards
item.dc:creator: Meghan Montemurro
item.description: Major League Baseball’s best defense earned hardware Sunday night. Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won the National League Gold Glove Award at their respective positions while three other finalists — left fielder Ian Happ, right fielder Seiya Suzuki and shortstop Dansby Swanson — fell short of the ultimate defensive honor. Milwaukee Brewers’ Jackson Chourio prevented Happ from winning his fifth straight Gold Glove Award in left field while the Arizo
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball’s best defense earned hardware Sunday night.
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman won the National League Gold Glove Award at their respective positions while three other finalists — left fielder Ian Happ, right fielder Seiya Suzuki and shortstop Dansby Swanson — fell short of the ultimate defensive honor.
Milwaukee Brewers’ Jackson Chourio prevented Happ from winning his fifth straight Gold Glove Award in left field while the Arizona Diamondbacks’ Corbin Carroll and Geraldo Perdomo finished in front of Suzuki, a first-time finalist, and Swanson.
The recognition is just getting started for Crow-Armstrong, who was voted Player of the Year and NL Outstanding Player by his peers league-wide last week — and he is expected to be named NL MVP next week. The 24-year-old won his first Gold Glove Award last year and should be considered the favorite to receive the Platinum Glove Award, which will be voted by fans and announced Friday.
Crow-Armstrong led all MLB outfielders with 26 outs above average (OAA) and a 26 fielding run value (FRV). His elite outfield coverage led to converting a remarkable 50% of five-star catch opportunities.
Bregman overcame a tough start to the season with shaky defense the first couple of weeks. He put in the work to earn his second Gold Glove Award, the other coming in 2024 during his last season with the Houston Astros. Among NL third basemen, his 7 FRV was tied for second-best while his 15 defensive runs saved led the majors at his position as one of only two third basemen to record double-digit DRS. Bregman also recorded the most assists by an NL third baseman.
Bregman is the first Cubs third baseman to win a Gold Glove Award since Ron Santo won the last of his five awards in 1968.
Chicago White Sox infielder Chase Meidroth was a finalist for the American League second base honor, which went to Cole Young of the Seattle Mariners. Meidroth led all AL second basemen in fielding run value (10) and was third in fielding percentage (.986) and outs above average (9), appearing in 150 games at the position.
— Chicago Tribune’s LaMond Pope contributed to this report.

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグ機構（ＭＬＢ）は１日（日本時間２日）、守備のベストナインにあたる「ゴールド・グラブ賞」を発表し、日本人選手の受賞はなかった。
日本人選手でゴールド・グラブ賞を受賞したのは、２００１〜１０年に１０年連続で受賞したイチロー（マリナーズ）だけ。１６年連続で受賞者なしとなった。１０月１４日（同１５日）に発表された各ポジションの最終候補３人には、ナ・リーグ右翼手部門でカブス・鈴木誠也外野手（３２）がベンジ（メッツ）、キャロル（ダイヤモンドバックス）とともに名を連ねていたが、受賞はならなかった。日本人選手が最終候補に入るのも２０年の投手・前田健太（ツインズ）、左翼手・秋山翔吾（レッズ）以来６年ぶりだった。
誠也は、広島時代にゴールデングラブ賞を外野で５度受賞。だが、カブスにはこれまで守備力の高い外野手も多かったことから、２５年は指名打者中心の起用だった。今季は正右翼手だったタッカーがドジャースに移籍して、右翼のレギュラーとなると、打撃だけではなく守備でも再三チームを救った。失策は「２」のみで、メジャー５年間で最も少なかった。１１１試合、９７２回３分の２、右翼の守備についた。守備機会２４２の失策２で、守備率は・９９２。右翼手の中ではトップの数字だった。誠也の右翼での守備率は２２年が・９８１、２３年が・９８７、２４年が・９８１、２５年が・９５１だったが、今季は一気に上昇した。
ＭＬＢのゴールド・グラブ賞は全３０チームの監督、コーチが自チームの選手以外に投票。その投票が７５％をしめ、残りの２５％は守備指標「ＳＡＢＲ」によって選出される。
誠也は今季限りで２２年に結んだカブスとの５年８５００万ドル（約１０１億円＝契約時のレート）が終了し、ＦＡとなった。４年連続で２０本塁打以上をマークし打撃力に加えて、守備力も兼ね備えていることから、今オフの外野手では目玉クラスの注目を受けている。

item.title: [日刊スポーツ] 鈴木誠也は岡本和真の同僚になる？複数の米メディアが有力移籍先にブルージェイズ - ＭＬＢ : 日刊スポーツ
item.description: カブスからFAとなった鈴木誠也外野手（32）について、複数の米メディアが移籍先に最も適した球団として岡本和真内野手（30）が所属するブルージェイズを挙げた。 ESPN電子版は30日付の記事で、今オフFA市場の目玉の1人と目される鈴木について「カブスでの5年間は、目を見張るほど安定して結果を出す打者だった」と称賛。「ブルージェイズは計算できる打線の中軸の獲得が必須。外野手兼DHのジョージ・スプリンガーとマイルズ・ストローがFAとなって抜けるため、その予算をスズキに使える」とした。 ニューヨークのスポーツ専門テレビ局SNY電子版も同日付の「今オフのFAトップ10」を特集した記事で、鈴木について「インパクトのある打者が市場に少ない中で、最も高評価になる可能性がある。右翼の守備でも強肩を発揮した」と称賛。ブルージェイズに入団すれば「今季不振に苦しんだウラジーミル・ゲレロをプロテクトする存在になるかもしれない」とした。これらメディアの予想通りなら、侍ジャパンのメンバーとして共にWBCを戦った2人がメジャーでもタッグを組むことになる。

item.content:encoded:
「すべてを凌駕するオファーを…」ドジャース、鈴木誠也獲得の可能性が高くなった！？ 米メディアが示唆「争奪戦になる可能性は高いが…」
2026.10.31 11:45 NEW
Getty Images
大谷翔平 最新情報
　ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが今オフ、テオスカー・ヘルナンデス外野手をトレードで放出した場合、その後釜としてシカゴ・カブスの鈴木誠也選手を獲得する可能性が浮上している。右打ちの長打力を補える存在として、鈴木への関心が取り沙汰されている。米メディア『ヘビー』のT.J.フレンチ記者が10月28日（日本時間29日）に言及した。
鈴木は今季、打率.270、本塁打26、打点86、安打147を記録。今オフでは日本からポスティングされて以降、初めてMLBのフリーエージェント（FA）市場に出る予定で、外野手では有力選手の1人とみられている。
そこで、来季のワールドシリーズ進出を目指すドジャースが獲得すべき選手として鈴木が挙げられた。ドジャースは有望株のホスエ・デポーラ外野手の出場枠を空けるためヘルナンデスを放出するとの見方がある一方、経験豊富な打者も補強したいとも考えている。
鈴木の市場価値については、4年総額1億700万ドル（約169億円）程度になると予想された。ドジャースであれば、この金額を出すことは問題ないだろう。
注目の集まる鈴木の動向についてフレンチ氏は「これはドジャースにとって十分に支払える金額であり、今オフに一部の契約金を帳簿から切り離すことができればなおさらだ。しかし、彼は争奪戦になる可能性が高いため、現実的にドジャースがそれらすべてを凌駕するオファーを出せるだろうか。それは、球団がこの32歳の外野手にどれほど強い関心を寄せているかにかかっている」と言及した。
ドジャースにはすでに大谷翔平選手という主軸がいるが、もし鈴木が加入となれば、日本人同級生として共闘することになる。ドジャース打線もさらに厚みを増すことになり、鈴木の去就に注目したい。

item.content:encoded:
カブスFAとなった鈴木誠也外野手（32）の移籍先候補として30日（日本時間31日）、「ESPN」がブルージェイズを最適球団に挙げた。昨季、岡本和真内野手（29）を補強したカナダ・トロントに本拠地を置く球団で、カブスとの再契約は「最優先事項にはならない」と見込んだ。
鈴木の評価について「5年間で驚くほど安定した打撃成績を残した。今季は予想外ともいえるほど優れた守備指標にも支えられ、WARで自己最高を記録。仮に守備面での好成績が一時的なものだったとしても、鈴木は打撃で得点を生み出せる選手」と好守で優れた能力を強調。だが、カブスは「補強資金を優先的に投入するのは先発ローテーションとなる見込み」とした。
昨年ワールドシリーズに進出するも、今季はア・リーグ最下位に沈んだブルージェイズは「外野陣のOPSが2025年のMLB7位から19位に低下し、戦力の底上げが必要。打線の中軸を任せられる安定した打者の獲得が不可欠となっている」と分析。他の移籍先候補にはタイガースを挙げ、「打線の新たな柱となる選手を獲得すべき。ライリー・グリーン、マックス・クラーク、鈴木で構成される外野陣を想像してみてほしい。デトロイトの来季の年俸総額は2026年と比べて約7000万ドル少なくなる見込みで、鈴木の獲得に加え、投手陣の補強にも資金を投入する余裕がある」と金銭的な余裕がある球団も候補になるとした。

item.title: [OCNJ Daily] Seiya Suzuki or Randy Arozarena, who would be a better fit for Phillies?
item.dc:creator: Tim Kelly
item.description: If you want the Phillies to sign either Seiya Suzuki or Randy Arozarena this winter, you’d better get comfortable with being uncomfortable. item.content:encoded:
If you want the Phillies to sign either Seiya Suzuki or Randy Arozarena this winter, you’d better get comfortable with being uncomfortable.
Suzuki and Arozarena — probably the top two bats available this offseason, and certainly the best outfield sticks — will both receive and decline qualifying offers. That means the Phillies would have to give up $1 million in international bonus pool money, along with their second- and fifth-round picks in the 2027 MLB Draft to sign either. That’s in addition to whatever it takes to sign either, with it very possible that both will require commitments of five years and at least $100 million.
Considering both Suzuki and Arozarena are entering their age-32 seasons and coming off of career years, there’s definitely a case to be made that the Phillies should look elsewhere for outfield help. Ian Happ — Suzuki’s long-time teammate with the Chicago Cubs — could be an alternative who requires a shorter commitment.
But for much, if not all, of this era, the Phillies have lacked right-handed thump in their outfield. Even if president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski doesn’t want to give five years to Suzuki or Arozarena, you can argue that the Phillies can’t afford to pass up on the opportunity to sign one of these two given how hard it’s proven to find a middle-of-the-order bat that’s right-handed and plays in the outfield in recent years.
The question then becomes, if the Phillies are going to take the plunge, which of the two would be better?
Seiya Suzuki’s Pros and Cons
The Cubs gave Seiya Suzuki a five-year/$85 million deal when he came stateside before the 2022 season, and he’s likely to get another half decade contract this offseason, but with a higher overall value this time around.
He hit .270 with 26 home runs, 86 RBIs, 81 walks and an .841 OPS in his contract year. While this was probably Suzuki’s best overall offensive season, he’s been pretty consistent at the plate over his five seasons. He’s recorded exactly 31 doubles in three of the last four seasons, including 2026. He’s a career .269 hitter with an .823 OPS, so it’s not like this year was a major outlier.
However, the reason Suzuki set a career-high with a 4.5 WAR this season — FanGraphs says his previous high water mark was 3.5 in 2024 — is because he made drastic defensive improvements. He played just 282 innings in right field in 2025, with the Cubs utilizing him mostly as a DH and occasionally left field when they had Kyle Tucker. But after Tucker departed in free agency, Suzuki returned to right field on a full-time basis. He went from posting minus-four defensive runs saved and minus-one out above average over 282 innings in right field in 2025 to 14 DRS and four OAA across 972 2/3 frames in 2026.
It’s a credit to Suzuki, and the fact that he’s a right fielder might make him slightly more valuable defensively than Arozarena. But that’s only if you buy his defensive improvement this past year, because the Phillies don’t have room for another DH.
Another interesting angle to Suzuki as a free agent is that the Phillies as an organization have been trying to establish a foothold in the Japanese market, a place they’ve clearly lagged behind other major spenders. The only two Japanese-born players to ever play for the Phillies are Tadahito Iguchi and So Taguchi, both of whom last suited up for the club in 2008. Signing Suzuki would get the monkey off the back of the Phillies, and potentially allow them to show future Japanese prospects that they are an organization who can support players who come from that portion of the world. Of course, that assumes things go well if they sign Suzuki. And it’s unclear if Suzuki would want that type of pressure.
Randy Arozarena’s Pros and Cons
For as disappointing of a season as the Seattle Mariners had as a team, Arozarena could be headed for a top-five finish in AL MVP voting. The former AL Rookie of the Year led the American League with 113 runs scored, while also homering 26 times, driving in 79 runs, drawing 68 walks and posting an .865 OPS. Arozarena’s season seems even more remarkable considering he played his home games at T-Mobile Park, which consistently grades out as one of the worst stadiums for hitters. Indeed, his OPS was .788 at home, as opposed to .933 on the road. It stands to reason that Arozarena’s season could have been even better if he was playing for pretty much any other team in the sport.
Arozarena’s agent, Scott Boras, will certainly point to that, along with the fact that Arozarena is a red-light player. With just 42 career regular season games under his belt, Arozarena set a new MLB single postseason record with 10 homers in the 2020 playoffs, helping the Tampa Bay Rays to win the pennant. He’s a showman, one whose personality would probably make him an immediate fan favorite in Philadelphia.
That’s the good, but where are the downsides? Arozarena was an A-level player in 2026. He’s been that for other portions of his career, although the .761 OPS he posted between 2022 and 2025 is more than 100 points lower than what he did in 2026. There’s a real chance Arozarena will get paid like an A-level player this offseason, but there’s definitely a risk that he proves be more like a B-level player over the lifetime of his contract.
The other drawback with Arozarena would be that he’s pretty much only a left fielder. In his career, he has minus-five defensive runs saved and minus-26 outs above average in left field. Citizens Bank Park is an easier outfield to patrol than T-Mobile Park or Tropicana Field, the two home parks he’s played in most of his career. But Arozarena has never been a great fielder, and he would be joining a team that finished tied for last in DRS in 2026 at minus-51. Plus, if he’s cemented in left field, that would limit the options the Phillies have with Trea Turner if he’s not able to convince them to keep him at shortstop.
Verdict
Suzuki is a safer bet offensively, but there’s probably a wider variance in defensive outcomes with him.
Arozarena, if successful, would be one of the most popular players the Phillies have ever had because of the swagger he plays the game with.
But if the Phillies are going to make an investment in another expensive veteran, they better be sure in what they are getting. Over his five MLB seasons, Suzuki has an .823 OPS. During that same period, Arozarena has a .782 OPS. Even if you factor in Arozarena spending the last two and a half seasons in Seattle, Suzuki’s bat gives him the edge.

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグ選手会が29日（日本時間30日）、2026年シーズン終了に伴ってFAとなった144選手を公表した。日本選手ではカブスFAの今永昇太投手（33）、鈴木誠也外野手（32）、ロッキーズFAの菅野智之投手（37）が公示された。
鈴木は2022年から結んだ5年契約を満了。今オフのFA市場では外野手が少なく、長打力を伴う鈴木は需要が高く大型契約が見込まれている。「ジ・アスレチック」のジム・ボウデン氏の予測では5年総額1億2000万ドル（約189億円）の新契約を予測。今永がクオリファイング・オファーを受け入れ1年契約を満了。同記事では3年総額6900万ドル（約108億円）を予測している。菅野は1年510万ドル（約8億円）の契約を終えた。
ドジャースはクリス・ブービッチ、ブラスダー・グラテロル、エンリケ・ヘルナンデス、エリック・ラウアー、エバン・フィリップス、ミゲル・ロハス（引退表明）、タリク・スクバル、ブレイク・トライネン、アレックス・ベシアの9選手が公示された。
今オフは米東部時間12月1日午後11時59分に労使協定が失効するため、MLBオーナー陣と選手会の交渉がまとまらない場合はロックアウトとなり、交渉を含めた移籍市場が凍結する可能性がある。

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグ選手会は29日（日本時間30日）、FA選手144人のリストを公表。日本選手ではロッキーズの菅野智之投手、カブスの今永昇太投手と鈴木誠也外野手の3人が入った。米報道によると、アストロズの今井達也投手は残り2年3600万ドル（約56億8000万円）の契約を破棄できるオプトアウトの権利を行使せず、来季のチーム残留を決断した。
11日に37歳を迎えた菅野はチームのエースとして29先発し、メジャー1年目だった昨季の10勝を上回る12勝（12敗、防御率5・37）をマーク。今季の年俸は昨季の1300万ドル（約20億5000万円）から510万ドル（約8億円）に下げたが、154回1／3を投げてチーム最多の勝ち星を手にした。
カブスの鈴木は5年8500万ドル（約134億3000万円）の契約を満了。5年目の今季は143試合に出場して、打率・270、26本塁打、86打点、OPS・841をマーク。3月のワールド・ベースボール・クラシック（WBC）で右膝を負傷したため、開幕を出遅れたが、打線の中軸として4年連続20本塁打をマークするなど、攻守でチームをけん引し、プレーオフ進出に大きく貢献した。
今オフは阪神からポスティングシステムを利用してメジャー移籍を目指す佐藤輝明内野手とともに野手最大の目玉として注目を集めている。
メジャー3年目の今永は自己最多の32先発＆174回1／3を投げて11勝10敗、防御率3・77をマーク。単年2202万5000ドル（約34億8000万円）のクオリファイングオファーを受諾して臨んだシーズンはローテーションの柱として先発陣を支えた。
大谷翔平、山本由伸、佐々木朗希の3投手が所属するドジャースからは9人がFAに。8月のトレード期限にタイガースから獲得したタリク・スクバル投手をはじめ、ベテランユーティリティのキケ・ヘルナンデス内野手、ブレイク・トライネン、アレックス・ベシア、エバン・フィリップス、クリス・ブービック、ブラスダー・グラテロル、エリック・ラウアーの6投手、すでに現役引退を表明しているミゲル・ロハス内野手がリスト入り。中でも2年連続サイ・ヤング賞を受賞している左腕のスクバルは今オフ、最大のFA選手と位置付けられている。

item.content:encoded:
今季終了後にカブスからフリーエージェント（FA）となる鈴木誠也外野手の去就が注目されている。米メディア『ジ・アスレチック』は26日（日本時間27日）、鈴木がカブスの想定を大きく上回る契約を手にする可能性を報道。チーム残留の難しさを指摘した。
■今季のQOは「2315万ドル」
『ジ・アスレチック』によると、今後カブスは鈴木に1年2315万ドル（約36億5千万円）のクオリファイングオファー（QO）を提示すると見られている。QOとはFAとなった選手に元所属球団が提示できる1年契約で、金額は今季年俸の上位125選手の平均と定められている。選手がQOを拒否して他球団と契約した場合、元所属球団には補償として条件に応じたドラフト指名権が与えられる。QOが拒否された元所属球団が、新たな複数年契約を提示することも可能だ。
鈴木は2022年からのメジャー5年間で、通算113本塁打を記録。今季は右翼手としての守備も評価を高め、ゴールドグラブ賞の最終候補にも入るなど、攻守で評価が急上昇している。
今オフのカブスは先発ローテーションの大幅な再編に加えて、捕手やブルペンも補強候補となっており課題が山積している。『ジ・アスレチック』は、人気銘柄の鈴木が「シカゴが快適に支払える金額を大きく超える契約を提示される」と分析。右の有力打者が少ないFA市場において、カブスが鈴木を引き留められない可能性が高まっていると見立てた。
同メディアは、現行の労使協定が12月1日（同2日）に失効するため、ロックアウト前の駆け込み需要でFA市場が一気に動く可能性もあると予想。鈴木の争奪戦は早期決着するのだろうか。

item.title: [CubsHQ] Seiya Suzuki projected to land massive $120 million contract
item.dc:creator: Tony Crumpton
item.description: Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki could be in line for a massive payday this offseason, with at least one team already generating buzz as a potential landing spot. Jim Bowden of The Athletic ranks Suzuki as the No. 6 overall free agent in his latest rankings and projects the 32-year-old outfielder to land a five-year, $120 million contract, averaging $24 million per season. Suzuki is coming off the best season of his MLB career, batting .270 with 26 home runs, 86 RBIs and a .368 on-base perce
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki could be in line for a massive payday this offseason, with at least one team already generating buzz as a potential landing spot.
Jim Bowden of The Athletic ranks Suzuki as the No. 6 overall free agent in his latest rankings and projects the 32-year-old outfielder to land a five-year, $120 million contract, averaging $24 million per season.
Suzuki is coming off the best season of his MLB career, batting .270 with 26 home runs, 86 RBIs and a .368 on-base percentage. He also posted a .473 slugging percentage, an .841 OPS and a 131 OPS+ while producing 5.1 WAR, according to Baseball-Reference.
While Suzuki has always been a productive offensive player, his improved defense in right field helped make 2026 his most complete season since arriving from Japan.
Rumors are growing that the Toronto Blue Jays will make Suzuki a priority this offseason as they look to strengthen their outfield and add lineup protection for superstar Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
Bowden lists Toronto and the Philadelphia Phillies as the two best potential landing spots for Suzuki.
The veteran outfielder has been one of Chicago's most consistent hitters since signing his original five-year, $85 million contract ahead of the 2022 season. Over his five seasons with the Cubs, Suzuki averaged more than 20 home runs per year and posted an OPS+ of at least 125 in each of the past four seasons.
His combination of offensive consistency, improved defense and experience makes him one of the more attractive position players available in free agency.
Bowden compared Suzuki's potential contract to several notable outfield deals, including Teoscar Hernández's three-year, $66 million agreement, Jung Hoo Lee's six-year, $113 million contract and Nick Castellanos' five-year, $100 million deal.
For the Cubs, Suzuki's projected price tag presents another difficult offseason decision.
Chicago already faces significant uncertainty in its outfield, with several players potentially departing through free agency. Losing Suzuki would create another hole in a lineup that ranked among baseball's most productive offenses in 2026.
At $24 million annually, bringing Suzuki back would require a big financial commitment from the Cubs, who also need to address their starting rotation and several other roster needs.

item.content:encoded:
鈴木誠也FA 最適球団は「ブルージェイズかフィリーズ」 5年189億円規模の交渉に 米報道
　MLBを取材するジム・ボウデン記者が27日（日本時間28日）までに、今オフのMLBフリーエージェント（FA）市場の目玉の1人、カブス・鈴木誠也外野手（32）について、移籍した場合の最適球団はブルージェイズかフィリーズとした。また、契約金は5年1億2000万ドル（約189億5000万円）に及ぶ可能性があると報じた。
鈴木は移籍市場でもトップクラスの高評価を受けており、今季も143試合、打率．270、26本塁打、86打点をマーク。チームのポストシーズン進出に貢献した。
カブスでの5年目のシーズンを終え、MLBで5年連続2桁本塁打、4年連続20本塁打以上と存在感は抜群。ブルージェイズには、「侍仲間」の岡本和真内野手、フィリーズには今季も両リーグトップタイの45本塁打をマークしたカイル・シュワバー外野手が在籍している。
どちらの球団に移籍しても、強力打撃陣の一角に組み入ることは間違いない。カブス残留の可能性も残されているが、その動向に関心は高まっている。

item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen

item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays and Seiya Suzuki have been paired as a match for months.
It's easy enough during a given MLB season to look at upcoming free agents from multiple rosters and figure out who might have openings and who might have money to spend.
The Blue Jays have basically aligned with Suzuki, the free agent outfielder from the Chicago Cubs, in every way.
They'd even have a chance for him to join his Japanese countryman, Kazuma Okamoto, who just had a solid debut season in Toronto.
Free agency hasn't officially arrived yet, but that hasn't stopped the rumor mills and speculation from continuing.
And the latest update for the Blue Jays and Suzuki continues to suggest that they could end up together.
Seiya Suzuki Blue Jays Update
The Athletic's Jim Bowden wrote on Tuesday that he sees the Blue Jays as one of the best fits for Suzuki in free agency.
Bowden notes the Philadelphia Phillies as the team Toronto could have to compete with, and it's worth adding that Bowden has the Phillies interested in Randy Arozarena, too, but not the Blue Jays. So if Philadelphia ended up with Arozarena, that could help the Blue Jays get Suzuki.
"There is a lot of scuttlebutt in the industry that the Blue Jays are going to be targeting him as they look to add more offense to their outfield and more protection in their lineup for Vladimir Guerrero Jr.," writes Bowden. "Suzuki was a consistent performer for the Cubs over the past five years, averaging over 20 homers per season and an OPS+ of at least 125 over the past four seasons."
After a season in which the Blue Jays missed the playoffs, they certainly won't want to go the entire offseason without making a splash. Suzuki would qualify, particularly in a weak free agent hitter market.
Given all the chatter, there's really no surprise that Bowden is linking Suzuki to the Blue Jays, too. They'll still have to close the deal at some point.
Seiya Suzuki Contract Projection
Bowden also provided a contract projection for Suzuki as part of his blurb. He predicts a five-year deal for $120 million, which would be $24 million per year.
"Suzuki is coming off the best year of his MLB career," Bowden writes. "He had a .270/.368/.473 slash line with 26 homers and a 131 OPS+. He not only ranked among the better hitters in batting run value, but he improved his defense in right to become an asset there as well."
In a better free agent class, Suzuki might fly under the radar. In this one, he's going to be one of the prized signings, and the Blue Jays sure seem to be hoping he can be theirs.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Blue Jays' Seiya Suzuki Update Says What Everyone Is Thinking appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
ポスティングシステムを利用してのメジャー挑戦が認められた阪神の佐藤輝明内野手（２７）は今オフのＦＡ市場でも大注目の存在だ。米スポーツサイト「ファンサイデッド」は２５日（日本時間２６日）に「佐藤は魅力な存在だが、カブスは手を出さない方が賢明だろう」と報じ、ＦＡになる鈴木誠也外野手（３２）と再契約すべきだと訴えた。
「佐藤はカブスにとって魅力的な選択肢であり、即戦力として攻撃力をさらに向上させる可能性を秘めているものの、必ずしもロースターにフィットするとは限らない」
佐藤は三塁が定位置で、外野の両翼を守ることができ、球団によってはホワイトソックスの村上のように一塁へコンバートする可能性もある。
カブスは三塁はブレグマン（２８本塁打、９３打点）、一塁はブッシュ（２０本塁打、７７本塁打）が守っており、入る余地はない。そうなると鈴木がＦＡ移籍した場合は右翼が空くが、同サイトは「カブスが佐藤の獲得を検討しているなら、鈴木と契約したほうが賢明だろう」と強調する。
理由はＭＬＢでの実績だ。鈴木は５年間カブスでプレーし、２年目の２３年から４年連続２０本塁打以上をマークし、通算１１３本塁打。今季のｂＷＡＲ５・１は移籍後最高だ。守備指標のＯＡＡ（平均的な選手と比べて何個アウトを多く取ったか）「５」はＭＬＢの右翼手５位で強肩も評価されている。
「もし、カブスが鈴木の代わりに佐藤を起用すれば、右翼という本来のポジションとは異なる守備位置での起用になり、ＭＬＢでの打撃が未知数な上にさらにリスクを負う」と警告した。
ブルージェイズが獲得に動くと報じられるなど鈴木もＦＡ市場で注目の存在だ。

item.content:encoded:
今季終了後にカブスからフリーエージェントとなった鈴木誠也外野手が、守備でも高い評価を受けた。米スポーツデータ会社『Sports Info Solutions（SIS）』が22日（日本時間23日）に発表した「フィールディング・バイブル賞」で、右翼手部門の3位にランクインした。
■守備指標が大幅改善
地元メディアも高評価
同賞は2006年に創設され、各守備位置の最優秀選手を選出。統計分析や目視評価などを基に、専門家らが投票する。今季の右翼手部門はウィルヤー・アブレイユ外野手（レッドソックス）が81ポイント、コービン・キャロル外野手（ダイヤモンドバックス）が53ポイントで1、2位となり、鈴木は43ポイントで3位にランクインした。
今季の鈴木は右翼手として111試合、972.2イニングに出場。MLB公式のデータサイト『Baseball Savant』によるOAA（Outs Above Average）が右翼手全体5位のプラス5を記録。一昨年のマイナス3、昨年のプラスマイナス0から大きく改善し、肩の強さと送球面での指標も優れていた。
今季は打撃だけでなく守備でも評価を高め、ゴールドグラブ賞の最終候補にも選出された。各球団の注目度は高く、人気銘柄の一人に挙がっている。

item.title: [CBS Sports] The state of the outfield position heading into 2027: Pete Crow-Armstrong leads a talented but thin field
